CaptureEraseResult.title: CaptureEraseResult
CaptureEraseResult.description:
What one erasure destroyed (or, previewing, would destroy) and what it leaves.

``would_erase`` answers a preview: nothing was erased or recorded, and
``erasure`` shows the record a commit would write (its instant is the
preview's). ``already_erased`` answers a Capture erased before: nothing new
is recorded and ``erasure`` is the existing record. ``citing_claims`` are
the live Claims that cite the Capture at the head; ``left_without_evidence``
those of them whose every cited Capture other than their own words would
then have an erased body (``next`` lists each as ``claim_evidence_erased``).
An erasure adds no rule of its own: verdicts read the evidence as no longer
replayable, and each ClaimType's own rules decide what that means (one that
requires current replay reads the Claim ``stale``). A live Claim citing an
erased Capture moves on by a re-bind onto a fresh Capture under the same
contract, and can be revised or retired: what it inherits verifies on the
envelope and this record (compiler revision 35).

subject.description: kind/<id, alias or single key value>, or {subject_kind, key} naming the Subject by its kind's key: the one live holder, else the one a subject member of the same change set creates (no id is predicted).

revises.title: Revises
revises.description: Claim ID this Claim revises; omit to state a new Claim.

ClaimInverse.title: ClaimInverse
ClaimInverse.description:
How a ClaimType states absence: the unit an inverse Claim covers and its evidence.

An inverse Claim (object ``{kind: none}``) says the unit ``key`` names holds
no value. Only a Capture one of ``evidence_rules`` admits can establish it,
whatever the type's ``evidence_requirement``. ``stale_after`` is how long an
inverse stays current (absent: the type's ``evidence_freshness``), so
absence can expire sooner than presence. ``description`` says what a none
means for this predicate.

ClaimInverseInput.title: ClaimInverseInput
ClaimInverseInput.description:
How the type states that a unit holds nothing.

``key`` names the unit: ``{kind: slot}`` for a one-valued type,
``{kind: object}`` or ``{kind: object_key, predicate}`` (a key ClaimType of
every object SubjectKind) for a many-valued one. ``evidence_rules`` are ids
of the type's own evidence rules, in any order; only a Capture one of them
admits establishes a none. ``stale_after`` takes ``P7D`` (absent: the type's
evidence freshness applies). ``tag`` may be left out; it is accepted so a
stored ClaimType's own inverse is also its input form.

ClaimInverseObjectKey.title: ClaimInverseObjectKey
ClaimInverseObjectKey.description: A many-valued unit is one object: its inverse says that object is not held.

ClaimInverseObjectKeyPart.title: ClaimInverseObjectKeyPart
ClaimInverseObjectKeyPart.description:
A many-valued, Subject-valued unit is one key part of the object Subject.

``predicate`` is a key ClaimType of every object SubjectKind; the inverse
says no object with that key value is held, whichever Subject has it.

ClaimInverseSlotKey.title: ClaimInverseSlotKey
ClaimInverseSlotKey.description: A one-valued slot's unit is the whole slot: its inverse says it holds nothing.

ClaimLine.title: ClaimLine
ClaimLine.description:
One Claim as a text line shows it: the Subject, the field, the value, the Claim.

Every surface that prints a line about a Claim (``since``, ``coverage
resolve``, ``audit``, refusals) carries this and renders it through
``get_display.render_claim_line``, so the line reads the same everywhere:
``subject  field[qualifier] = value  [CLM-<12 hex>]``. ``subject`` is
``kind/id``; ``field`` is the short field name ``get`` and ``orient`` show;
``value`` is the summary value (a long string is a ``TruncatedText``
preview). Digests and artifact paths stay in the typed record beside it.

ClaimPrecedence.title: ClaimPrecedence
ClaimPrecedence.description: Highest role first; one policy governs every Procedure replacement.

ClaimQueryResult.title: ClaimQueryResult
ClaimQueryResult.description: One replayable canonical read of accepted Claim state.

retires.title: Retires
retires.description: Claim ID this member retires, parallel to revises.

ClaimRetirementMember.title: ClaimRetirementMember
ClaimRetirementMember.description:
One attributed Claim retirement, closure and all, as a change-set member.

`mode` is `submit` alone: a change-set member is authored inside an intent
whose own preflight already reports the closure this member still owes, so
the second, member-local preflight mode of the standalone retirement route
would only name the same inventory twice.

`retires` is the bare Claim ID, named and spelled exactly as
`ClaimAuthoringPayload.revises` is. Tolerating a `Claim:` prefix here would
give two spellings of one retirement the same member identity but different
payload digests, so create-dedup would miss and two live intents could carry
one semantic identity.

ClaimStatementCard.title: ClaimStatementCard
ClaimStatementCard.description: Flat, typed statement-first projection shared by read and floor surfaces.

ClaimStatementProcedureMeasurement.title: ClaimStatementProcedureMeasurement
ClaimStatementProcedureMeasurement.description: Test one exact accepted Claim statement's evidence-relative verdict.

ClaimType.title: ClaimType
ClaimType.description:
The one ClaimType: what a predicate means, admits and settles.

Optional members are omitted from the wire when absent, so absence and a
stated value never share a spelling.

ClaimTypeAuthoringPayload.title: ClaimTypeAuthoringPayload
ClaimTypeAuthoringPayload.description:
One whole ClaimType definition authored inside an ordinary change set.

A succession -- a ClaimType that names a predecessor, and the migration its
whole reverse-pin closure then owes -- is `ClaimTypeSuccessionMember`, a
member of its own, because the closure is the decision. This member defines
a ClaimType nothing yet depends on.

ClaimTypeContention.title: ClaimTypeContention
ClaimTypeContention.description:
How a ClaimType settles rival Claims of one slot, as a read shows it.

``selector`` is its resolution policy's: ``only_contender`` (a one-valued
slot is answered by its single eligible Claim) or ``all`` (every eligible
Claim of a many-valued slot answers). ``on_conflict`` is what a one-valued
slot with rival contenders resolves to: ``unresolved`` (the slot stays
conflicted until one is retired) or ``refuse``. ``corroboration`` and
``freeze`` count its admission policy's corroboration and freeze
requirements, omitted at zero.

ClaimTypeInputRecord.title: ClaimTypeInputRecord
ClaimTypeInputRecord.description:
One ClaimType, as authored: state what differs from the defaults.

A new ClaimType states ``predicate`` and ``cardinality``. The predicate's
prefix before its last dot supplies ``allowed_subject_kinds``; state it for
a multi-kind field. ``value`` declares a native Contract field type;
omitted, it is ``string{max_len: 256}``. Subject-valued fields state
``subject<K>`` or ``subject<K1 | K2>``. Prose belongs in Documents.
Every other field takes its default, written out in full in the stored ClaimType
(``cruxible claim-type propose --template --expanded`` prints them):

- ``permitted_roles``: ``[default_role]`` when one is stated, else
  ``[normative]``.
- ``evidence_admission_policy``: with ``evidence_requirement`` ``self`` (the
  default) or ``none``, one own-words rule (``self``, contract
  ``cruxible.coordinator-self-source-v1``) for every permitted role but
  ``derivation``, which also admits workspace file and section citations;
  plus, for ``evidence: [<contract>, ...]``, one rule admitting those shaped
  contracts (derivationally for ``derivation``); with ``captured``, the
  ``evidence`` rules only.
- ``admission_policy``: no corroboration or freeze requirements.
- ``resolution_policy``: supported, current Claims; ``only_contender``
  (one) or ``all`` (many); a conflict leaves the field unresolved.
- ``evidence_requirement``: ``captured`` for exactly ``[observation]``
  (which requires a source or explicit evidence policy), otherwise ``self``.
  ``revision_evidence``: ``replace``.
- ``canonical_form``: ``[nfc, trim]`` for string literals, enum included;
  state ``[]`` for no transforms. Other object types have no default form.

An edit (a predicate this instance already holds) follows JSON merge-patch
(RFC 7396) against the accepted predecessor for every field but
``predicate``: a field left out keeps the predecessor's value, so an
unrelated edit never drops what the type means or how it is backed. An
explicit ``null`` clears a field that may be empty (``evidence_freshness``,
``attestation_consequence_policy``,
``unsure_hold_for``, ``description``, ``member_descriptions`` (``[]`` too),
``default_role``, ``canonical_form``, ``inverse``); the others always have a value, so
they are named or left out, never ``null``. Durations (``evidence_freshness.stale_after``,
``unsure_hold_for``) take ISO-8601 (``P30D``) or ``{microseconds: N}``.
A rule names a contract by its public or stored name.

ClaimTypeLintWarning.title: ClaimTypeLintWarning
ClaimTypeLintWarning.description: One advisory finding about a ClaimType's evidence policy, with its fix.

ClaimTypeMemberDescription.title: ClaimTypeMemberDescription
ClaimTypeMemberDescription.description: What one literal enum member means, beside the ClaimType that admits it.

ClaimTypeMemberDescriptionInput.title: ClaimTypeMemberDescriptionInput
ClaimTypeMemberDescriptionInput.description: What one literal enum member means; lowering normalizes and sorts these.

ClaimTypeSuccessionDependent.title: ClaimTypeSuccessionDependent
ClaimTypeSuccessionDependent.description:
What one member of a succession's closure becomes in the same generation.

The vocabulary is the standalone migration route's own, so an author who
knows one road knows the other: `successor` carries the dependent to the
successor type by re-pinning it, `retire` tombstones it -- with
`claim_retirement_reason` `was-rescinded` that is a rescission, with any
other reason and an optional `claim_effective_until` it is an ordinary
attributed retirement.

`re_author` is the disposition only a change set can offer: the dependent's
successor is a sibling Claim member of the same intent, named by
`successor_claim_id` -- the Claim ID that member revises, which is this
dependent's own. That sibling is lowered under the successor type, so it may
say under the new vocabulary what the predecessor could not say -- and it
keeps the dependent's identity, its subject and its predicate, and its exact
predecessor digest, which is what makes it a re-authoring of that Claim
rather than a new one. There is no second spelling by member index: an index
could only ever name the member this Claim ID already names.

carry_all.title: Carry All
carry_all.description: Carry every closure member dependents does not name to the successor, computed by the daemon (retired Claims included); dependents then names only exceptions.

retire_dependents.title: Retire Dependents
retire_dependents.description: Retire every live Claim of the closure dependents does not name, with this reason, and carry the rest; what retiring a ClaimType (a retired successor) owes its dependents.

ClaimTypeSuccessionInput.title: ClaimTypeSuccessionInput
ClaimTypeSuccessionInput.description: Succeed one accepted ClaimType, and disposition its closure, in this set.

ClaimTypeSuccessionMember.title: ClaimTypeSuccessionMember
ClaimTypeSuccessionMember.description:
One ClaimType succession, its whole closure disposed, as one member.

Evolving a committed vocabulary is one epistemic move -- "I need this
distinction, and here is everything it changes" -- so it is one member of
one change set, and it admits or refuses with the Claims that speak the new
vocabulary rather than days after them.

`successor` is a whole ClaimType that names its predecessor by identity and
pins its exact digest, which is what makes it a succession rather than the
definition `ClaimTypeAuthoringPayload` carries. A retired successor retires
the ClaimType; its live Claims must then retire with it
(`retire_dependents`). `dependents` is the exact reverse-pin closure of the
predecessor over the staged tree -- the accepted tree as this set's
definition members left it -- and a closure that is not exact refuses.
Sibling Claims are not in it: members lower in dependency order, so a Claim
of the succeeded predicate authored in this same set is lowered under the
successor and lands as an ordinary member.

ClaimsExpectByEnd.title: ClaimsExpectByEnd
ClaimsExpectByEnd.description:
``expect: {by, ends}``: the run is complete for these ends of the pair part ``by``.

The row Subject is a pair kind; ``by`` names one of its Subject-valued key
parts (by predicate or short name) and ``ends`` references the list of
those ends (text references or structured rows, as ``expect`` names
Subjects). The pairs judged are those of each end that hold a live fact
of a template's ClaimType, found through the pair index; each is then
judged from its own Claims by the ordinary absence gates.

ClaimsExpectBySpec.title: ClaimsExpectBySpec
ClaimsExpectBySpec.description: Absence by one end of a pair row: the run is complete for ``ends`` of part ``by``.

ClaimsRunSummary.title: ClaimsRunSummary
ClaimsRunSummary.description:
One claims terminal: what it wrote, kept, retired, surfaced and skipped.

``written`` and ``revised`` count new and revising Claims, ``inverse_written``
the declared-inverse Claims (written or revising) apart from them, and
``subjects_created`` the Subjects created by key. ``re_observed`` counts
held Claims a new Capture re-confirmed and whose re-observation was
recorded; ``reobservations_refused`` counts, by reason, the ones whose
re-observation the record refused (the Claim is unchanged, but its content
was not observed again). ``no_op`` counts restatements that changed
nothing at all. ``downgraded`` counts values written as the ClaimType's
unknown member over incomplete input. ``surfaced`` counts held Claims a
source no longer contains that were reported instead of retired;
``skipped`` counts the other findings, by kind (an item not written, or an
incomplete source). ``delivery`` is how the change landed.

CompilerCoordinate.title: CompilerCoordinate
CompilerCoordinate.description:
Validated semantic compiler/schema coordinate outside the bootstrap preimage.

``implementation`` names the reference semantics whose rule digest is
accepted. The physical assembler engine that realizes those semantics is
recorded separately as nonlogical projection build metadata.

CompilerUpgradeNotice.title: CompilerUpgradeNotice
CompilerUpgradeNotice.description:
What sets a compiler upgrade apart from every other proposal: it is one-way.

Carried by the upgrade's preview, its proposal and its review, where the
decision to activate is made. Once activated, the accepted head names
``target_compiler_digest``, and a release whose daemon does not install
that compiler can no longer serve the instance; there is no downgrade.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

ConsumerStatus.title: ConsumerStatus
ConsumerStatus.description: One daemon consumer on one instance: an enabled Line, or a built-in worker.

Contract.title: Contract
Contract.description:
One immutable data shape. A successor version names its predecessor's digest.

``fields`` may be empty: the closed empty record, which accepts only ``{}``
(an empty selector, a refusal without detail, a parameterless operation).

ContractAuthoringPayload.title: ContractAuthoringPayload
ContractAuthoringPayload.description:
One Contract version: a named, immutable data shape.

``fields`` are typed by the Contract grammar. Lowering writes
``contracts/<name>/v<version>.json``, pins each nested ``name@N`` to the
accepted version's digest, and names version N-1 as the predecessor of
every later version. An accepted version never changes; author the next.

ContractEvidence.title: ContractEvidence
ContractEvidence.description: This contract's newest verified exact-bytes Capture about the Subject.

ContractField.title: ContractField
ContractField.description: One field: its type, whether its key may be absent, and what it means.

type.title: Type
type.description: The field type, e.g. 'string', 'int{0..9}', 'decimal{0..1}', 'date', 'enum[open, fixed]', 'list<string>{max_items: 50}', 'key<security.vulnerability>', 'capture<security.kev>', or another Contract as 'name@N'. A trailing '?' makes the key optional (absent, never null).

ContractFieldInput.title: ContractFieldInput
ContractFieldInput.description: One Contract field with its meaning: a type spelling and an optional description.

version.title: Version
version.description: The version this declares, starting at 1.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Field name to its type spelling, or to {type, description}. Empty ({}) declares the closed empty record, which accepts only {}.

ContractInput.title: ContractInput
ContractInput.description:
One Contract version: a named, immutable data shape every edge is checked against.

Each field has a type from the closed grammar: there is no ``json`` type and
no untyped map (keep opaque bytes as a Capture), and every list states
``max_items``. Nested Contracts are written ``name@N`` and pinned to the
accepted version. Version 1 starts a Contract; version N names version N-1
as its predecessor. An accepted version never changes: author the next.

ContractRef.title: ContractRef
ContractRef.description: A pin to one Contract version. Authors write ``name@N``; acceptance adds the digest.

CountOperand.title: CountOperand
CountOperand.description: The number of elements of the referenced list (guards and repeat ``until`` only).

CoverageCardBudget.title: CoverageCardBudget
CoverageCardBudget.description: §11.6.4: candidate cards stay conservatively budgeted and say when clipped.

CoverageResult.title: CoverageResult
CoverageResult.description:
One resolved coverage answer: the whole `playbill-coverage-result-v1`.

``result`` carries the frozen coverage grammar verbatim -- span results,
cards, the one batch summary, coverage health, accepted coordinate, scope,
manifest epoch, and the index/overlay/manifest digests the answer was
resolved against. Coverage remains reproducible from those three digests;
a successful outer read may additionally append a local consumption touch,
which enters neither this answer nor accepted state.

CoverageScanBudget.title: CoverageScanBudget
CoverageScanBudget.description: The bound on relocation scanning, in bytes fed through SHA-256.

CoverageSelection.title: CoverageSelection
CoverageSelection.description: The byte window of a working source a caller is asking about.

subject_kind.title: Subject Kind
subject_kind.description: The kind, as orient names it.

key.title: Key
key.description: One value, {field: value}, or [{"predicate", "value"}]; none if minted.

create_new.title: Create New
create_new.description: Hint kinds only: create another live holder of the key.

expect_new.title: Expect New
expect_new.description: Refuse subject_exists if the key has a live holder.

role.title: Role
role.description: The key Claims' role, when the key field permits more than one.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: What the key Claims cite, as a set's evidence: a section (one this write appends: its text is the author's own words), a file, a Capture, or self. Default: the write's `because`.

CreateChange.title: CreateChange
CreateChange.description: Create a Subject by kind and key, or land on its one live holder; core assigns ids.

value.title: Value
value.description: A Subject-valued part takes kind/id or {created: label}.

CreateKeyPart.title: CreateKeyPart
CreateKeyPart.description: One key part of a create: a literal, or (a pair's end) a Subject.

CreatedSubject.title: CreatedSubject
CreatedSubject.description: A create change of this write, by its label, in any order.

expression.title: Expression
expression.description: Five fields, minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, evaluated in UTC. Cron expressions are evaluated in UTC; convert local times first (09:00 New York in winter is 14:00 UTC).

CronSchedule.title: CronSchedule
CronSchedule.description:
Fire at each instant a standard five-field cron expression names, in UTC.

``minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week``, always read as UTC: no host
timezone database enters an instant, and a schedule names no timezone. The
Trigger law refuses an expression the grammar does not admit; see
``cruxible_client.contracts.cron``.

DecimalType.title: DecimalType
DecimalType.description: A decimal; bounds are canonical decimal strings, never floats.

DeclaredBlockPageObservation.title: DeclaredBlockPageObservation
DeclaredBlockPageObservation.description:
One workspace page's stamped blocks as a client read them, for block-churn detection.

The daemon never reads the workspace, so `block sync` and `block repin`
send what they read of each page they touched: its digest, and each
stamped block's marker summary (stamp, body digest, byte window).

DocConfirmationOutcome.title: DocConfirmationOutcome
DocConfirmationOutcome.description: One landed edit's history confirmation; no refusal means it was recorded.

DocEditObservation.title: DocEditObservation
DocEditObservation.description:
Bounded wire observation of an edit; carries no workspace path or locator.

``section`` labels the resulting subtree. ``before_digest`` is absent for a
new child. Whole-file coordinates support client-side compare-and-set;
the daemon never opens the file they describe.

confirmation.title: Confirmation
confirmation.description: Pending edit to confirm only after the local file write succeeds.

DocOutcome.title: DocOutcome
DocOutcome.description: The client's section result; citing-Claim reports are deferred.

target_identity.title: Target Identity
target_identity.description: A kind-qualified identity: Subject:kind/id, ClaimType:p, Procedure:n, …

DocumentShell.title: DocumentShell
DocumentShell.description: Canonical light envelope; body bytes remain outside the ledger.

key.title: Key
key.description: The canonical key, in key order.

DuplicateKeyGroup.title: DuplicateKeyGroup
DuplicateKeyGroup.description: Subjects of one ``hint`` kind that hold the same canonical key.

DuplicateSubject.title: DuplicateSubject
DuplicateSubject.description: One Subject in a group, with the names (its id and aliases) that met.

key.title: Key
key.description: The broad comparison's spelling the names share.

DuplicateSubjectGroup.title: DuplicateSubjectGroup
DuplicateSubjectGroup.description: Subjects of one kind whose ids or aliases meet under the broad comparison.

DuplicateValue.title: DuplicateValue
DuplicateValue.description: One live Claim holding one of the values that met.

key.title: Key
key.description: The broad comparison's spelling the values share.

canonical_form.title: Canonical Form
canonical_form.description: The predicate's declared canonical form, under which they differ.

DuplicateValueGroup.title: DuplicateValueGroup
DuplicateValueGroup.description: Values of one predicate equal under the broad comparison, distinct as stored.

DuplicatesAuditRequest.title: DuplicatesAuditRequest
DuplicatesAuditRequest.description: One page of the duplicates audit for one Subject kind.

git_oid.title: Git Oid
git_oid.description: The accepted coordinate the audit read.

budget_exhausted.title: Budget Exhausted
budget_exhausted.description: The audit stopped reading at its bound; groups past it are not listed.

DuplicatesAuditResult.title: DuplicatesAuditResult
DuplicatesAuditResult.description: One page of possible duplicates of one kind, for an agent to resolve.

keys.title: Keys
keys.description: Key Claims of a hint kind read.

DuplicatesAuditScanned.title: DuplicatesAuditScanned
DuplicatesAuditScanned.description: The work one audit did: what it read, counted.

EgressRunSummary.title: EgressRunSummary
EgressRunSummary.description:
One ``emit_capture`` or ``post_inbox`` terminal: the items it emitted.

``unposted`` counts the items a post's inbox cap left out.

EnumOfType.title: EnumOfType
EnumOfType.description: The members a ClaimType's enum value admits, read from that ClaimType.

EnumType.title: EnumType
EnumType.description:
A closed set of string members.

``ordered`` (compiler revision 74) declares the members in ascending rank:
the first is lowest, the last highest. Queries then compare and order the
stored member strings by that rank; values are never remapped. Unordered,
the field is omitted from the canonical bytes, so existing digests hold.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Structured error payload returned by the HTTP server.

ExactContentObjectInput.title: ExactContentObjectInput
ExactContentObjectInput.description:
The exact bytes a Claim's object IS, spelled as text or as base64.

`text` is the ordinary spelling and stays the ordinary spelling: rulings and
method laws are prose, and prose typed into JSON should not have to be
encoded first. `content_base64` is for the bytes text cannot carry -- a body
that is not valid UTF-8, or one whose exact bytes matter more than its
reading -- and is the same spelling the SDK's own `ExactContent` lowers to,
so the two doors put identical bytes in the ledger.

Exactly one of them, because two spellings of one body are two bodies the
moment they disagree, and the digest is over the bytes.

ExistingCaptureCitationSource.title: ExistingCaptureCitationSource
ExistingCaptureCitationSource.description: Reference one already-materialized Capture without re-authoring its bytes.

ExtractCompleteWhen.title: ExtractCompleteWhen
ExtractCompleteWhen.description:
An extract's declared count check, bounded for a summary.

``count_at`` is the declared path, cut to ``NODE_SUMMARY_TEXT_MAX`` code
points (``count_at_truncated`` then says so). ``expected`` is absent when
the source enumerated no count; a count past ``NODE_SUMMARY_INT_MAX`` is
left out and ``out_of_range`` says so.

ExtractField.title: ExtractField
ExtractField.description:
Where one field is read, and how its lexeme becomes a typed value.

``at`` is a JSON Pointer relative to the record (or to the document, for a
header field), or a CSV column name. ``parse`` converts a text lexeme
(``date``, ``datetime``, ``int``, ``decimal``, ``bool``); ``type`` states
the field's type where no row Contract does (keys and header fields);
``canonicalize: claim_type`` matches an enum member case-insensitively.
``presence`` overrides the row Contract's optionality. ``project`` reshapes
the parsed value: ``utc_date`` (``parse: datetime``) keeps its UTC calendar
day; ``utc_start_of_day`` (``parse: date``) is that day at 00:00 UTC.

ExtractRunSummary.title: ExtractRunSummary
ExtractRunSummary.description:
One extract: the records it read, and what its completeness rests on.

``records`` counts every record read, ``invalid_records`` and
``duplicates`` those among them that were invalid or a refused duplicate;
``invalid_fields`` counts the invalid field results of valid records.
``complete_when`` is the declared count check's result, when one is declared.

file.title: File
file.description: PATH#ANCHOR: a workspace file and text found once in it; the write catalogues the file if it is not yet.

observation.description: Filled by the client that read the file; leave it out.

FileEvidence.title: FileEvidence
FileEvidence.description: File evidence sent as bytes by the client; the daemon never reads workspace files.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

FloorDeliveryResult.title: FloorDeliveryResult
FloorDeliveryResult.description: The same floor delta and write receipt returned by a daemon delivery.

FloorDelta.title: FloorDelta
FloorDelta.description:
What brings a floor at ``base_generation`` to ``head``.

``kind="full"`` carries every file and no base; a receiver replaces its
floor. ``kind="delta"`` carries the files whose ``changed_at`` is after the
base, and ``tombstones``, the base's paths the head no longer has. Both are
a deterministic function of (head, base) for one renderer.

FloorDeltaFile.title: FloorDeltaFile
FloorDeltaFile.description: One file the base lacks or holds at different bytes.

FloorDeltaRequest.title: FloorDeltaRequest
FloorDeltaRequest.description:
Ask for what brings a floor at ``base_generation`` to ``at`` (default: head).

``base_generation`` and ``base_renderer`` come from the client's own floor
manifest; with either absent the answer is the whole floor.

FloorExport.title: FloorExport
FloorExport.description:
The deterministic greppable floor as base64 bytes keyed by floor path.

``manifest`` is the decoded root ``manifest.json``: it binds every file to
the accepted coordinate it was projected from. The service is
filesystem-free, so materializing the directory is the client's act.

FloorHead.title: FloorHead
FloorHead.description: The accepted coordinate a delta brings a floor to, and its generation.

GenerationAcceptedSchedule.title: GenerationAcceptedSchedule
GenerationAcceptedSchedule.description: Fire once at the latest accepted head after it moves, coalescing a burst.

GetApprovalPolicyCard.title: GetApprovalPolicyCard
GetApprovalPolicyCard.description: The instance's approval policy: whether a proposer may approve its own change.

event.title: Event
event.description: The attestation door event's digest, for a recorded event.

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: The consequence-policy rule it counts under.

GetAttestationEvidence.title: GetAttestationEvidence
GetAttestationEvidence.description:
One attestation of this exact Claim version, and whether it counts.

An accepted attestation artifact, or an event ``claim attest`` recorded.
The verdict reads accepted ones: a current one counts when it cites
Captures the Claim admits. Either counts when the ClaimType's consequence
policy has a rule for its stance. A recorded event is otherwise shown and
resurfaced in ``next``, never read by the verdict (``not_accepted``).

target.title: Target
target.description: What the links point into, as resolved.

GetBacklinks.title: GetBacklinks
GetBacklinks.description:
``detail="backlinks"`` (D-R32): one page of the pointers into the reference.

The same rows as the ``backlinks`` read: notes and Documents ``about`` a
Subject and the sections its live Claims cite; the Documents that ``guides``
a ClaimType or Procedure.

subject_suggestions.title: Subject Suggestions
subject_suggestions.description: SDK-internal: suggest nearest Subject names when resolution fails. World sets false to bound absent Subject lookups to the identity indexes. Other kinds retain their ordinary suggestions.

GetBatchRequest.title: GetBatchRequest
GetBatchRequest.description:
Several references read at one coordinate and one detail: an SDK-internal route.

Agents call ``get`` once per reference; the SDK reads a whole vocabulary
(every ClaimType envelope, for ``world()``) in a few round trips with this,
and resolves individual World Subjects without population-wide suggestions.
Every result answers the coordinate the first one resolved.

GetBody.title: GetBody
GetBody.description: A byte range of one Document body; ``body_digest`` names the whole body.

GetCapabilityCard.title: GetCapabilityCard
GetCapabilityCard.description: One capability version: an immutable kind of call a Procedure slot names.

GetCaptureCard.title: GetCaptureCard
GetCaptureCard.description:
A retained Capture: its contract, when it was observed, and who cites it.

``status`` is whether the store can still produce it, as the evidence
worker last saw (``status_detail`` names the defect); ``read_capture``
verifies and reads its material, behind body-read permission.

GetCaptureDerivation.title: GetCaptureDerivation
GetCaptureDerivation.description:
A derived Capture's recorded inputs (D-R37 d5): the Captures and state reads it
was computed from, and its reducer. ``get`` each source to follow the chain.

GetCaptureErasure.title: GetCaptureErasure
GetCaptureErasure.description: Who erased a Capture's retained body, when and why.

capture.title: Capture
capture.description: Capture handle, CAP- plus the digest's first 12 hex; get and read_capture accept it.

version.title: Version
version.description: Accepted version of that contract the capture used.

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: Whose bytes the citation reads: an independent source's, the Claim's own authored words (self_source), or a legacy backing's.

status.title: Status
status.description: admitted: the ClaimType's rule admits it and the verdict reads it; not_admitted: offered as evidence, refused by the rule; not_evidence: a copy the rule does not admit, which the verdict never reads.

byte_length.title: Byte Length
byte_length.description: How many bytes the Capture holds, from its commitment (no body read); absent when it commits to no exact bytes or is withheld from this reader.

erased.description: Present when the Capture's retained body was erased: its bytes are gone, so the verdict reads this evidence as no longer replayable.

passage.title: Passage
passage.description: The bytes of this Capture the Claim maps (its cited spans), as proposal review shows them; absent when it maps none, the body is withheld, erased or unavailable.

passage_truncated.title: Passage Truncated
passage_truncated.description: The passage was cut at the review's cited-text limit.

GetCaptureReducer.title: GetCaptureReducer
GetCaptureReducer.description:
What computed a derived Capture: the provider build, operation and its node's input.

``provider`` and ``operation`` name what the digests pin: the build's
``Provider:NAME/BUILD`` reference (absent when no accepted Provider has
that artifact) and the operation the Capture's invocation called.

GetChangeSetReason.title: GetChangeSetReason
GetChangeSetReason.description:
Why this revision was proposed: the rationale of the change set that accepted it.

A write's ``because`` (with any per-retire note), or an authored change
set's rationale, read from the exact admission the accepted generation
published. Provenance, not evidence. Over ``GET_REASON_MAX_CHARS`` it is
cut (``truncated``); ``get <proposal>`` reads it whole.

GetContractCard.title: GetContractCard
GetContractCard.description: One Contract version: an immutable data shape, field by field.

GetContractField.title: GetContractField
GetContractField.description: One Contract field: its type as authors spell it, and what it means.

GetCoordinate.title: GetCoordinate
GetCoordinate.description: Which accepted generation answered: the git oid's 12-hex prefix and its sequence.

GetDocumentLink.title: GetDocumentLink
GetDocumentLink.description: One of a Document's own links: its relation and the identity it names.

GetEndPairs.title: GetEndPairs
GetEndPairs.description:
The pairs a Subject is an end of through one key part of one pair kind, in id order.

A pair is listed when it holds a visible fact: a live, positive, supported
and current Claim (a query's default visibility at the read's instant). A
pair whose facts are all hidden (not yet effective, expired, stale,
contradicted) is counted in ``hidden``; one whose facts are all retired is
a historical shell, reached through ``incoming``.

GetEvidenceRule.title: GetEvidenceRule
GetEvidenceRule.description: One evidence rule: which roles it admits evidence for, under which contracts.

GetFieldChanged.title: GetFieldChanged
GetFieldChanged.description: A revision with a new value; ``before`` is the value it replaced.

GetFieldRebound.title: GetFieldRebound
GetFieldRebound.description:
A re-bind: the same statement, with drifted citations replaced by new ones.

``replaced`` are the Captures (``CAP-<12 hex>`` handles) whose citations the
revision dropped; ``by`` the Captures it cited in their place. The Claim ID
and lineage stay; ``reason`` is the write's ``because``.

GetFieldReobserved.title: GetFieldReobserved
GetFieldReobserved.description: A revision with the same value on new backing (evidence refreshed).

GetFieldRetired.title: GetFieldRetired
GetFieldRetired.description: The Claim's retirement: the field no longer holds ``value``.

GetFieldStated.title: GetFieldStated
GetFieldStated.description:
A new Claim lineage: the field's first value, one more of a many-valued field,
or (``contended``) a competing value beside a live one of a single-value field.

GetGuidance.title: GetGuidance
GetGuidance.description: A governed Document linked ``guides`` a ClaimType or Procedure (D-R17).

GetHistory.title: GetHistory
GetHistory.description:
One page of revisions, newest first; ``revision`` counts from the oldest.

Each revision's value follows the summary card rule: a string over 500
characters is a ``TruncatedText`` preview whose ``read_whole`` reads this
revision's whole value at its own generation.

GetIncoming.title: GetIncoming
GetIncoming.description:
One page of the live Claims pointing at a Subject, in Claim id order.

Read through the object index one page at a time: a page costs its rows,
never the Subject's whole incoming set. ``get`` each Claim (or batch them)
for its verdict and value.

GetIncomingClaim.title: GetIncomingClaim
GetIncomingClaim.description:
One live Claim whose Subject-valued object is the Subject read.

``subject`` is the asserting Subject (``kind/id``): a relation is stored
once, on it, so this is the edge read from its object's side.

GetKindEnd.title: GetKindEnd
GetKindEnd.description: One Subject-valued key part of a pair kind: its key ClaimType and the end's kind.

GetLineEnablement.title: GetLineEnablement
GetLineEnablement.description: One enablement of a Line: who enabled it, and what its automation is doing.

GetLineOccurrence.title: GetLineOccurrence
GetLineOccurrence.description: One pending occurrence: ``due`` once its window has closed, else ``waiting``.

GetLineRuns.title: GetLineRuns
GetLineRuns.description:
One page of a Line's Procedure runs, newest admission first.

Read through the run journal's per-Line partition index one page at a
time, keyed by each admission's immutable position: a run admitted or
finished between pages is never repeated or skipped, and a page costs its
rows, never the Line's whole run history. Runs are operational state, read
live at the current head. ``get ProcedureRun:<run>`` reads one.

GetLineTrigger.title: GetLineTrigger
GetLineTrigger.description: One live Trigger aimed at a Line: its name, accepted version and when it fires.

GetMandateCard.title: GetMandateCard
GetMandateCard.description:
One mandate: what it grants, to which exact Line, over what, and until when.

``scope`` lists the ClaimTypes a settle grant covers; ``subject_scope`` the
Subjects it is limited to (artifact paths), absent when it reaches every
Subject its namespace does; ``condition`` the settlement predicate;
``subject_creation`` the Subject kinds a settle may create. ``suspended``
appears only when the mandate's kill switch is on. ``line`` is the Line it
grants, at the exact version it pins (``Line:<name>@<digest>``).

GetNone.title: GetNone
GetNone.description:
One none in a field: a live inverse Claim saying the field holds nothing.

``of`` is the unit it covers: absent for a one-valued field's whole slot,
else the value (a Subject as kind/id) or key value the field does not hold.

GetNoteCard.title: GetNoteCard
GetNoteCard.description: One note: a workspace section linked ``about`` Subjects (never a Claim).

note.title: Note
note.description: NOTE-<32 hex>; get reads its card.

drift.title: Drift
drift.description: Has the section moved since it was linked?

GetNoteLink.title: GetNoteLink
GetNoteLink.description:
A note about a Subject, as a pointer to its section: never the section's prose.

``cruxible section FILE#Heading/Path`` (FILE the path the catalog maps
``file`` to) reads the section itself.

GetNotes.title: GetNotes
GetNotes.description: ``detail="notes"``: one page of the notes about a Subject, as section pointers.

GetPairEnd.title: GetPairEnd
GetPairEnd.description: One end of a pair Subject: the key part that names it and the Subject it names.

GetPairs.title: GetPairs
GetPairs.description:
One page of the pairs a Subject is an end of, by pair kind and key part.

Read through the pair index one page at a time: a page examines at most
twice its ``limit`` plus eight candidate pairs, never the Subject's whole
set of pairs nor any other Subject's. Hidden candidates are counted per
group, never listed; a page may hold fewer rows than ``limit`` while
``truncated`` says more candidates follow.

proposal.title: Proposal
proposal.description: The proposal's ID; get and proposal review read it.

GetPendingProposal.title: GetPendingProposal
GetPendingProposal.description: An open proposal that would write fields of the Subject: not accepted state yet.

GetPredictionWindow.title: GetPredictionWindow
GetPredictionWindow.description: One bound window of a ResolutionContract, as the settlement worker holds it.

GetPrincipalCard.title: GetPrincipalCard
GetPrincipalCard.description: One registered principal: who it is, what kind, and whether it is active.

GetProcedureNode.title: GetProcedureNode
GetProcedureNode.description: One node the direct run lane does not execute, and where it can run.

GetProcedureRuntimePolicyCard.title: GetProcedureRuntimePolicyCard
GetProcedureRuntimePolicyCard.description: The instance's Procedure runtime ceilings: how much one run may produce and retry.

first_sequence.title: First Sequence
first_sequence.description: The first run record the promotion covers.

last_sequence.title: Last Sequence
last_sequence.description: The last run record the promotion covers.

output.title: Output
output.description: The reducer's output over those records, as accepted.

GetProcedureTrackRecord.title: GetProcedureTrackRecord
GetProcedureTrackRecord.description:
One accepted promotion of a Procedure's run exhaust, and what it computed.

A promotion pins a contiguous range of run records and a reducer; its
acceptance makes the reducer's output over exactly those records part of
accepted state. Records nobody promoted are never counted here.

GetProposalRefusal.title: GetProposalRefusal
GetProposalRefusal.description: One refusal diagnostic of a refused proposal, with its served repair.

GetProposedReason.title: GetProposedReason
GetProposedReason.description:
Why this revision was proposed, in its own Procedure item's words.

Read from the proposal that accepted the revision: the item's own
``rationale``, and the run and terminal that proposed it. Provenance, not
evidence.

GetProviderCard.title: GetProviderCard
GetProviderCard.description: One accepted Provider build, using the names shown by provider list.

digest.title: Digest
digest.description: Artifact digest prefix of this revision.

GetRevision.title: GetRevision
GetRevision.description:
One accepted revision of the thing ``get`` names, and why it was proposed.

A Claim's revision says what it did (``change``) and, when retired, why it
ended (``retirement``); ``reason`` is the shared resolver's: the Procedure
item's own reason for it, else its change set's rationale, else absent.

GetRunListMember.title: GetRunListMember
GetRunListMember.description:
One member of a call's ``list<capture>`` output, as the run journaled it (D-R37 a).

``index`` orders the list; ``request`` is the member's identity (the request
digest its coordinate carries). ``status`` is core's acquisition decision:
``selected`` (committed), ``omitted`` (dropped; the list is then
incomplete) or ``refused``; ``reason`` is its first reason code.

GetRunNode.title: GetRunNode
GetRunNode.description:
One node that finished, in journal order.

``duration_us`` is absent: the journal records every event of a run at the
run's evaluation instant (the deterministic clock), so per-node durations
are not derivable from it. ``summary`` is what flowed through a node that
succeeded (its records, rows, Captures, branch or Claim counts), by kind;
it is absent for a node that refused or failed, and for a kind that keeps
none (``project``, ``select``, ``invoke``).

GetRunOutcome.title: GetRunOutcome
GetRunOutcome.description: One durable outcome a finished run recorded.

GetRunTrigger.title: GetRunTrigger
GetRunTrigger.description: What admitted a Line run: the Line, its occurrence, and the enablement that dispatched it.

GetRunbookCard.title: GetRunbookCard
GetRunbookCard.description:
One Runbook (D-R36): its steps, the Triggers aimed at it and its recent runs.

Steps and Triggers are definitions at the read coordinate; the runs are its
retained run records, read live, newest first, each with every step's outcome.

GetRunbookStep.title: GetRunbookStep
GetRunbookStep.description: One step of a Runbook: its target and whether it can run now.

GetSubjectHistory.title: GetSubjectHistory
GetSubjectHistory.description:
A Subject's history: its shell's revisions, and one page of its field events.

``revisions`` are the Subject shell's own (created, pins, retired), all of
them, or none when the read names a ``field``. ``events`` are its fields'
changes, newest first, one page: each revision of each Claim about the
Subject, with what it did and why. Group them by ``field`` for each field's
value timeline.

GetSubjectKindCard.title: GetSubjectKindCard
GetSubjectKindCard.description: One SubjectKind: how core names and identifies Subjects of the kind.

GetTriggerCard.title: GetTriggerCard
GetTriggerCard.description: One Trigger: when it fires and what it sets off.

GitWorkspaceNote.title: GitWorkspaceNote
GitWorkspaceNote.description: Client-side advisory when CWD wins over inherited Git selectors.

GuardNode.title: GuardNode
GuardNode.description:
Branch on a closed run predicate (the same typed Predicate transforms use).

``refusal_code`` and ``message`` are the abort diagnostic: present exactly
when an arm is ``$abort``.

GuardOperand.title: GuardOperand
GuardOperand.description:
One comparison a guard evaluated: its operator, and its numeric or bool operands.

An operand that is anything else (a string, a list, a record) is left out;
so is the whole comparison when neither operand is a number or a boolean.
A number past ``NODE_SUMMARY_INT_MAX`` is left out too, and ``out_of_range``
says so. ``present`` and ``absent`` carry whether the reference resolved as
``left``.

GuardRunSummary.title: GuardRunSummary
GuardRunSummary.description: One guard: the branch it took, and the numeric and bool operands it compared.

GuardStep.title: GuardStep
GuardStep.description:
Branch on a typed run predicate.

``then`` (default: continue with the next step) and ``else`` (default:
abort ``guard_refused``) are typed actions.

HaltAction.title: HaltAction
HaltAction.description: End this branch successfully without a result; ``id`` names the halt node.

HaltNode.title: HaltNode
HaltNode.description: A successful graph leaf that deliberately produces no result.

HaltRunSummary.title: HaltRunSummary
HaltRunSummary.description: One halt: the reason code it declares, when it declares one, cut to the text bound.

Head.title: Head
Head.description:
The accepted head (or the coordinate ``at`` names) and its generation.

The cheapest read there is: no kind, artifact or attention fold, only the
coordinate a caller pins its next reads to and the generation a floor's
freshness is counted in. Internal callers use it in place of ``orient``.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

HostInspection.title: HostInspection
HostInspection.description: Credential-safe compatibility view of one governed daemon host.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

HostWorkspaceAttachResult.title: HostWorkspaceAttachResult
HostWorkspaceAttachResult.description:
One daemon host attached to a folder (Git or not), before or after its init.

An initialized host attaches a plain folder, or a Git worktree in the
ledger's own Git object format, that holds no part of the host's managed
root; nothing is rebuilt. ``already_attached`` answers the folder the host
already has (its ledger mirror is rebound). ``would_attach`` answers a
preview, which registered nothing.

HostWorkspaceRegistration.title: HostWorkspaceRegistration
HostWorkspaceRegistration.description: Whether one daemon host has a daemon-local workspace registration.

InboxAcknowledged.title: InboxAcknowledged
InboxAcknowledged.description: An agent saw the item and owes it nothing further.

InboxDismissed.title: InboxDismissed
InboxDismissed.description: An agent judged the item needs nothing, and said why.

InboxDispositionResult.title: InboxDispositionResult
InboxDispositionResult.description: The item after a disposition. ``recorded`` is false when it repeated the current one.

InboxEgressNode.title: InboxEgressNode
InboxEgressNode.description:
Terminal output into the Line inbox: typed items sent, as they are, to intelligence.

Every posted item is a record of ``contract`` (an accepted Contract,
``name@N``, pinned to its digest). With ``for_each`` (a reference to a list
the run produced: an extract's or a closed transform's records, a rows
view, or any list) each element posts one item whose ``fields`` read it as
``$item...`` (``$item.fields.<f>`` reads a record's field when it is
present); without it, ``fields`` resolve to one item. ``dedupe_key`` names
the item fields that are its identity in the inbox: items with the same
key are one item (absent: the whole item). Posting is inert: it never
touches accepted state. ``max_items`` caps what one run posts
(``INBOX_RUN_ITEM_CAP_DEFAULT`` when absent); items past it are not posted
and the run reports the truncation.

InboxItem.title: InboxItem
InboxItem.description:
One inbox item whole: envelope, the payload exactly as posted, and its latest decisions.

``recent_dispositions`` holds the latest ``INBOX_RECENT_DISPOSITIONS``,
newest first; the envelope's ``disposition_count`` says how many there
were in all, and the inbox journal keeps every one.

InboxItemEnvelope.title: InboxItemEnvelope
InboxItemEnvelope.description:
The core envelope of one inbox item: everything about it except its payload.

``occurrences`` counts every run that posted the item. ``first_sighting`` is
the earliest of them and ``recent_sightings`` the latest
(``INBOX_RECENT_SIGHTINGS`` at most, newest first), each with the Captures
its posting stood on. ``disposition`` is the agent's latest decision, kept
when the item recurs: a recurring item keeps its status, and
``recurred_since_disposition`` counts the sightings after that decision.

InboxLinkProposal.title: InboxLinkProposal
InboxLinkProposal.description: Link an item to the proposal an agent wrote about it.

InboxLinkSubject.title: InboxLinkSubject
InboxLinkSubject.description:
Link an item to a Subject (``kind/id``, or ``kind/<alias or key value>``).

The daemon records the Subject it resolves to, as ``kind/id``.

InboxLinked.title: InboxLinked
InboxLinked.description: An agent recorded where its judgment of the item lives: a proposal or a Subject.

InboxList.title: InboxList
InboxList.description: One page of inbox items, most recently posted first.

InboxListEntry.title: InboxListEntry
InboxListEntry.description:
One listed item: its envelope and a bounded preview of its payload.

``payload_preview`` follows the summary-read conventions: a long string is a
``TruncatedText``, an object a ``ShownObject``. A payload whose canonical JSON
runs past the summary bound is shown as a ``TruncatedText`` of that JSON
text. ``inbox get`` returns the whole payload.

InboxPostTruncation.title: InboxPostTruncation
InboxPostTruncation.description:
A ``post_inbox`` terminal selected more items than its run may post.

``cap`` is the terminal's declared ``max_items`` (``cap_source="declared"``)
or the core default; a run posting from more than one terminal counts them
together. The first ``posted`` of the ``selected`` items were posted; the
rest were not posted anywhere.

InboxSighting.title: InboxSighting
InboxSighting.description: One run's posting of an item, and the Captures that item's closure reached in it.

InboxStep.title: InboxStep
InboxStep.description:
Post typed items to the Line inbox: ``inbox`` names the item Contract, ``name@N``.

``for_each`` references a list the run produced (each element posts one
item, read with ``item`` references); ``fields`` make the item;
``dedupe_key`` names the fields that are an item's inbox identity.

InitBaseKit.title: InitBaseKit
InitBaseKit.description:
The base kit creation installs: ``accepted`` at once, or ``proposed`` under
independent approval, with the proposal that awaits a second approver.

InstalledProvider.title: InstalledProvider
InstalledProvider.description: One live provider build at the accepted head: what it runs and implements.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

InstanceDecommissionRequest.title: InstanceDecommissionRequest
InstanceDecommissionRequest.description: The operator's stated reason for ending this instance's governed writes.

InstanceDecommissionResult.title: InstanceDecommissionResult
InstanceDecommissionResult.description: Receipt for the terminal lifecycle state of one governed instance.

InvokeNode.title: InvokeNode
InvokeNode.description: A call to a named accepted Procedure under the enclosing run's limits.

params.title: Params
params.description: The child's parameter values, over its defaults (its params Contract).

KeyPartType.title: KeyPartType
KeyPartType.description:
``key_part<K:part>``: one key part of kind ``K``, canonicalized by that part's rule.

``part`` names the key ClaimType by predicate or by its last name under the
kind (``key_part<security.vulnerability:cve_id>``).

KeyType.title: KeyType
KeyType.description:
A Subject key of one kind; core canonicalizes it with the kind's identity rule.

The value is the key: the bare value for a one-key kind, or a mapping of
every key part to its value for a composite one (canonically keyed by each
part's last name under the kind; a conversion also reads full predicates).
Core canonicalizes each part with its key ClaimType's canonical form and the
SubjectKind's normalizer for it.

KeyTypeOverride.title: KeyTypeOverride
KeyTypeOverride.description: The one override a node may make: a Subject key type for a plain-string key part.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

KitAddRequest.title: KitAddRequest
KitAddRequest.description:
Install or upgrade a kit. It always proposes: a conflicting definition takes
the release's version unless kept, and a replaced definition's dependents are
carried to it.

KitArtifact.title: KitArtifact
KitArtifact.description: One artifact a kit carries, named by its accepted path and exact digest.

KitAutomationTemplate.title: KitAutomationTemplate
KitAutomationTemplate.description:
The kit's automation template, as ``kit build`` checks and carries it (D-R48).

One authoring change set of Lines, Triggers, Mandates and Runbooks, at
``path`` inside the kit. It is an inert file: never installed, never
submitted by ``kit add`` or an upgrade. The adopter tailors it (Line names,
sources, cron times, Mandate expiries) and submits it as their own change.

KitBuildProvider.title: KitBuildProvider
KitBuildProvider.description:
A provider package to name in the kit, staged in the body store: the built
wheel, the uv lock it was built with, and the wheels of the dependencies that
lock names by path (``provider install WHEEL --lock FILE`` takes the same three).

``delivery`` ``index`` makes it the kit's default provider: the kit records
the package, version, wheel and lock digests and carries none of the files,
and ``kit add`` installs it by name from the consumer's provider index when no
Provider there serves its operations. The staged wheel must be the
published build and the lock the one it embeds.

KitBuildRequest.title: KitBuildRequest
KitBuildRequest.description:
Export this instance's definitions under ``owns`` as one kit release.

``providers`` bundles provider packages with the release (the same wheels
this instance installed), so the kit's Lines can bind their operations.

KitBundle.title: KitBundle
KitBundle.description:
A manifest and the exact bytes of every artifact it names.

``provider_files`` holds the bundled provider packages' bytes, or nothing: a
bundle sent to ``kit add`` carries none, because the adapter stages each file
in the daemon's body store first.

KitChangeResult.title: KitChangeResult
KitChangeResult.description: What a kit add or remove changed, or why it changed nothing.

KitDocumentBody.title: KitDocumentBody
KitDocumentBody.description: One governed Document body a kit carries, named by its CAS digest.

KitFile.title: KitFile
KitFile.description:
One inert file a kit release carries for its reader: never a definition.

Kit files are not part of the release identity (``content_digest``), so a
docs fix leaves every definition digest and KitReceipt as it was; ``kit add``
never sends them to the daemon.

KitIdReusedRefusal.title: KitIdReusedRefusal
KitIdReusedRefusal.description: An installed kit id cannot silently become an unrelated set of prefixes.

KitKeptDivergence.title: KitKeptDivergence
KitKeptDivergence.description:
A definition the consumer kept its own way on purpose, so upgrades do not re-ask.

``release_digest`` is the release's version it declined (None for a definition
the release dropped); a later release that changes that definition again asks
once more.

KitOwnershipConflictRefusal.title: KitOwnershipConflictRefusal
KitOwnershipConflictRefusal.description: Another installed kit owns an overlapping prefix or holds a definition.

KitPathPlan.title: KitPathPlan
KitPathPlan.description: One kit definition in a change: what happens to it and what that does here.

KitProvenance.title: KitProvenance
KitProvenance.description:
Where a release was built: claimed by the builder, not proven.

Shown by kit status and the install preview; it is not part of the release
identity, so the same definitions built twice are the same release.

KitProvider.title: KitProvider
KitProvider.description:
One provider package a kit names: its built wheel and the uv lock it was
built with, plus the wheels of the first-party dependencies that lock names by
path. Registry dependencies are never bundled: the daemon resolves them by
name from its provider index (PyPI unless the operator configured one),
pinned by the lock's hashes.

A bundled package (the default delivery) is carried as those files; ``kit
add`` installs it before the kit's definitions, through the ordinary
transfer install, so the operations it declares are there for the kit's Lines
to bind. An ``index`` package is the kit's default provider of its
operations: the kit carries no file of it, ``kit add`` installs ``package``
at exactly ``version`` by name (its lock is the one the wheel embeds, its path
dependencies come from the same index) unless another live Provider here
already serves every one of its operations' signatures, and ``wheel`` and
``lock`` name the published build it verifies.

KitProviderFile.title: KitProviderFile
KitProviderFile.description:
One file of a bundled provider package, by name and exact sha256.

The sha256 is also its body-store digest: ``kit add`` reads the file from the
daemon's body store under it, where the CLI and MCP adapters stage it.

KitRecipeParamSpec.title: KitRecipeParamSpec
KitRecipeParamSpec.description:
One parameter of a kit recipe: its type, whether it is required, its default.

``kit adopt --param NAME=VALUE`` sets it; the recipe file names it as
``{{NAME}}`` inside a JSON string value. A string that is exactly
``"{{NAME}}"`` takes the typed value (an integer or boolean stays one);
embedded in a longer string it is spelled as text (``true``/``false``).

KitRecipeSpec.title: KitRecipeSpec
KitRecipeSpec.description:
One recipe a kit declares: a parameterized change set at ``path`` (a
``recipe`` file of the kit) that ``kit adopt KIT:NAME`` renders and submits
as the adopter's own governed change. ``default`` is what ``kit adopt KIT``
selects. Inert, like every kit file: never installed by ``kit add``.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

KitRequirement.title: KitRequirement
KitRequirement.description: One kit this kit requires, at ``min_version`` (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) or later.

KitRequirementStatus.title: KitRequirementStatus
KitRequirementStatus.description: One kit an installed kit requires, and whether this instance meets it.

KitResumeStatus.title: KitResumeStatus
KitResumeStatus.description:
A ``kit add`` that stopped at awaiting_providers and resumes on activation, or
one that stopped at its proposal (creation's base kit under independent approval).

KitScriptSpec.title: KitScriptSpec
KitScriptSpec.description:
One script a kit declares: Python at ``path`` (a ``script`` file of the
kit) that ``kit run KIT:NAME`` verifies against the installed release and runs
client-side with the ``cruxible python`` environment, never in the daemon.

LayoutExtractNode.title: LayoutExtractNode
LayoutExtractNode.description:
Read one record set of a Capture through its kind's layout (stored node).

``capture`` is ``$steps.<alias>.<field>`` as on today's node; ``records``
names a record set; ``header`` lists header fields, sorted. ``row`` is the
record set's row Contract pin ``{name, version, digest}``, added when the
Procedure is accepted (ruling L1; never authored): every later read takes that
row and only its fields, so a kind whose row grew does not change what the
accepted Procedure extracts.

LayoutRecordSet.title: LayoutRecordSet
LayoutRecordSet.description:
One named record set: where its records are, their key, row Contract and field rules.

``count_at`` names a document field that states how many records the set
holds; a read is complete only when it equals the records read.

LedgerMirror.title: LedgerMirror
LedgerMirror.description:
Where one instance publishes its ledger, and whether that copy is current.

`ledger set-mirror` binds a remote and waits boundedly for initial publication;
`orient` shows the URL and `next` its health. A publish barrier is acknowledged when
published_sequence reaches wait_sequence, even if newer work is pending. The
URL carries no credential -- one that could is refused before it is stored --
so this model is safe to print, log and hand to anyone who may read the
instance at all.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

LedgerMirrorClearRequest.title: LedgerMirrorClearRequest
LedgerMirrorClearRequest.description: Stop publishing to the bound mirror. Commits by default; preview with dry_run.

LedgerMirrorCleared.title: LedgerMirrorCleared
LedgerMirrorCleared.description:
The mirror an instance stopped publishing to, or would stop on a preview.

Clearing calls nothing back: what was already sent stays on the remote.
``already_clear`` answers an instance that had no mirror bound.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

LedgerMirrorRequest.title: LedgerMirrorRequest
LedgerMirrorRequest.description: The remote this ledger publishes to. Never a URL carrying a credential.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

LedgerPublishRequest.title: LedgerPublishRequest
LedgerPublishRequest.description: Wait at most this many seconds for the configured mirror to acknowledge.

LineAcquisitionRule.title: LineAcquisitionRule
LineAcquisitionRule.description: One capture output's rule as a Line declares it.

LineAuthoringPayload.title: LineAuthoringPayload
LineAuthoringPayload.description:
Decision-only Line input; lowering owns the exact Procedure and binding pins.

An author names the accepted or same-set Procedure by name; lowering pins
its exact version. ``bindings`` names a ``provider[/build]#operation`` (or
a ``provider[/build]`` whose one fitting operation is meant) per slot, keyed
by slot, or ``<invoke node path>.<slot>`` for an invoked child; a slot left
out is fitted through the signature index (exactly one live operation must
serve its signature). Lowering records the exact ``{build, operation}``.
``acquisition`` declares the acquisition rule per capture output
(``<alias>.<field>``); one it leaves out runs under the stated core default.
A budget left unset lowers to the Procedure's own hard caps.
``parameters`` is the Procedure's input record, checked against its input
Contract when the Line lowers. When the Line runs is not its own: Triggers
aim at it. ``trigger_input`` binds the triggering Capture to one capture
output, ``<alias>.<field>``, and lowering declares the exact event it accepts.

LineBudgetsInput.title: LineBudgetsInput
LineBudgetsInput.description: The budget a Line author states; each unstated required limit defaults to the cap.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.description: Continue after the last occurrence a previous page attempted (its `cursor`), so occurrences that stayed blocked are not attempted again.

retry.title: Retry
retry.description: Explicitly retry one closed or blocked occurrence against the current Line version in the same epoch, while its Trigger still aims at the Line unchanged.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: What this enable or disable call did. `already_enabled` and `already_disabled` changed nothing.

coordinate.description: The accepted coordinate this enable or disable call evaluated the Line at. Commit a preview with at=<its git_oid>.

LineEnablement.title: LineEnablement
LineEnablement.description:
One Line's automatic dispatch: enabled forward-only, or why it stopped.

An enabled Line admits the occurrences its daemon matched since it was
enabled or last restarted, under the pinned Line version, the exact Trigger
versions aimed at it when it was enabled, and the enabling credential. A
Trigger aimed at a Line does nothing until the Line is enabled. Occurrences
matched before a restart, or by explicit evaluation, stay pending for
explicit dispatch.

LineEnablementPrincipal.title: LineEnablementPrincipal
LineEnablementPrincipal.description:
Who enabled a Line: the authority rechecked before every automatic admission.

``runtime_credential`` retains only the credential's identifier, never a
token. On an auth-off daemon, ``principal_claim`` is an enablement made under
a configured principal ID (``label``), whose accepted standing is rechecked
before every admission; ``local_operator`` is the implicit local operator
that claimed no principal, and never resolves to a registered principal.

since.title: Since
since.description: Reads VALIDITY WINDOW. inclusive eligibility bound.

until.title: Until
until.description: Reads VALIDITY WINDOW. exclusive eligibility bound, capped at daemon time.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: Report what the range makes eligible without enqueueing it (read-only).

LineEvaluateRequest.title: LineEvaluateRequest
LineEvaluateRequest.description:
Evaluate a Line's Triggers over a range: enqueue what they make eligible, or preview it.

Evaluation records pending occurrences for explicit dispatch and never runs
anything. ``dry_run`` only reads: it reports the occurrences without
enqueueing them, so it needs no range and no governed write.

LineEvaluateResult.title: LineEvaluateResult
LineEvaluateResult.description: One evaluation's result: ``pending`` is current state, ``newly_enqueued`` is this call's.

bindings.title: Bindings
bindings.description: Slot -> 'provider[/build]#operation' (or 'provider[/build]'); an invoked child's slot is '<invoke node>.<slot>'. Omitted slots are fitted.

acquisition.title: Acquisition
acquisition.description: Per capture output <alias>.<field> (an invoked child's: <invoke node path>.<alias>.<field>): {max_age, on_unavailable, on_stale, on_oversized, permitted_replayability, origins}. A capture output left out runs under the core default: any age, refuse when unavailable, stale or oversized, any replay class, any origin.

max_authority.title: Max Authority
max_authority.description: Caps this Line below its Procedure's own capability; omit to inherit it.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: The Procedure's params: values over its params defaults, checked against its params Contract at authoring.

budgets.description: Per-run budgets; omit to use the Procedure's hard caps.

LineInput.title: LineInput
LineInput.description:
One Line: a stable instantiation of an accepted or same-set Procedure.

Lowering pins the named Procedure's exact version and binds every slot to
one exact ``{build, operation}``: ``bindings`` names
``provider[/build]#operation`` (or ``provider[/build]``) per slot, and a
slot left out is fitted (exactly one live operation must serve its
capability). A Line runs when run explicitly (`line run`, one manual occurrence),
or, once it is enabled (`line enable`), when a Trigger aimed at it fires; a
Trigger aimed at a Line that is not enabled does nothing. Enabling needs
governed write even for an observe-only Line. A Line that proposes or
settles also needs a live ProcedureMandate pinning this exact Line before it
can run or be enabled; an observe-only Line needs none.

LineOpenProposalOutcome.title: LineOpenProposalOutcome
LineOpenProposalOutcome.description:
How a Line run's proposal terminal stood to its Line's open proposal.

``still_current``: the run's change equals the open proposal's (the same
statements on the same evidence content, the same retired Claims and the
same created Subjects), so nothing was proposed -- no change; open proposal
``proposal_id`` still current. ``superseded``: the change differed, so the
run's own proposal was submitted and open proposal ``proposal_id`` was
withdrawn as superseded by it. Nothing carries over to the new proposal.

repeat.title: Repeat
repeat.description: Run on an event the enabled Line already admitted, deliberately again.

evaluation_time.title: Evaluation Time
evaluation_time.description: Reads EVALUATION INSTANT. An assertion only: the occurrence's instant is the daemon clock's, and an assertion outside the ProcedureMandate skew bound refuses.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Per-run values over the Line's parameters (checked against the Procedure's params Contract). A run whose parameters differ from the Line's runs without the Line's mandate: it may propose, never settle. Triggers always run on the Line's own parameters.

LineRunRequest.title: LineRunRequest
LineRunRequest.description:
One manual run of an accepted Line, now: never a Trigger's occurrence.

The run uses the Line's own inputs, budgets, authority ceiling and mandate
and is recorded on its history. ``event`` is the retained Capture event a
Line whose Procedure takes an event input runs on; one the enabled Line
already admitted refuses unless ``repeat`` says to run it again.

LineTarget.title: LineTarget
LineTarget.description: Run one Line, whatever version of it is accepted when the Trigger fires.

LineTriggerBinding.title: LineTriggerBinding
LineTriggerBinding.description:
Semantic cause of one occurrence, independent of its dispatch instant.

``trigger`` is the Trigger artifact that fired. A cadence or cron tick binds
no event or window: its instant is the occurrence's own evaluation instant.

LineTriggerVersion.title: LineTriggerVersion
LineTriggerVersion.description: One exact version of a live Trigger aimed at a Line.

LiveHead.title: LiveHead
LiveHead.description: The accepted head a live read was taken at: its git oid's 12-hex prefix and sequence.

LiveView.title: LiveView
LiveView.description:
Marks the parts of an answer read live: operational state has no history.

``as_of`` is the current head those parts were read at, which differs from
the answer's own coordinate when the read named an older ``at``; ``fields``
names what was read live (``card`` when the whole card is).

LogicalSourceIdentity.title: LogicalSourceIdentity
LogicalSourceIdentity.description:
The stable logical source a coverage answer is keyed on.

Not a filesystem path, not a line number, not a byte offset, and not a
content digest: those are all presentation or content, and §11.6.1 needs an
identity that survives an edit. Two planes exist because accepted state has
exactly two locator-free ways to name a source -- a ledger artifact path and
a registered external `source_identity`. A CAS reference deliberately has no
logical source: it is addressed by its content, so identical bytes found
anywhere are the same object and the question "which source is this?" has no
answer to give. Working sources that have no accepted counterpart at all
enter as `external` under a declared identity; the adapter that knows the
filesystem declares the binding, and the resolver never sees a path.

MandateChangeScope.title: MandateChangeScope
MandateChangeScope.description: The evidence bases one change kind of a scoped ClaimType settles on.

MandateChanges.title: MandateChanges
MandateChanges.description: Per change kind, the bases a settle grant covers; a kind left out never settles.

MandateConditionAuthoring.title: MandateConditionAuthoring
MandateConditionAuthoring.description: The settle predicate, named by query; lowering pins the exact accepted query.

MandateConditionView.title: MandateConditionView
MandateConditionView.description:
The accepted query that is a settle grant's settlement predicate.

Core binds ``binding_parameter`` from each target's binding referent; every
other parameter is fixed in ``fixed_parameters``. A target settles only on
one complete, conflict-free row with every ``required_fields`` value
present; otherwise the grant does what ``fallback`` says.

MandateScope.title: MandateScope
MandateScope.description:
One ClaimType a settle grant covers.

``claim_type`` is its ``ClaimType:<predicate>`` ref, ``changes`` the
change kinds the grant may settle on it with the evidence bases each
settles on, ``value`` an enum or bool ClaimType's allowed moves, and
``binds`` which referent of the changed Claim (its ``subject`` or its
``object``) binds the condition query's parameter.

MandateScopeAuthoring.title: MandateScopeAuthoring
MandateScopeAuthoring.description:
One ClaimType a settle grant covers, named by predicate; lowering pins its digest.

``changes`` lists, per change kind, the evidence bases that settle
