(``{create: {basis: [extracted]}, retire: {basis: [absence]}}``); ``value``
limits an enum or bool ClaimType's moves (``{from: [...], to: [...]}``).

MandateValueCondition.title: MandateValueCondition
MandateValueCondition.description:
Enum and bool ClaimTypes only: the values a settled change may move from and to.

``from`` lists the held values a change may replace (a create holds none, so
it settles only when ``from`` is omitted); ``to`` the values it may write (a
retirement or an inverse writes none, so it settles only when ``to`` is
omitted). At least one is declared.

Membership.title: Membership
Membership.description: ``left`` is (``in``) or is not (``not_in``) one of the literal members or a list.

NamePair.title: NamePair
NamePair.description: One stored identity (or prefix) and the name a reader sees for it.

NamedCaptureContract.title: NamedCaptureContract
NamedCaptureContract.description:
The stored CaptureContract (format v4).

``decoding`` is optional: it declares how the bytes decode for an
``extract``, and a Procedure whose extract reads a CaptureContract without
it is refused when it is accepted. ``layout`` is optional too: the header
fields and named record sets the kind's documents carry, which an extract
names. A kind without one renders exactly as before.

NestedType.title: NestedType
NestedType.description: A field holding one record of another Contract version.

capture.title: Capture
capture.description: The newest Capture, which no Claim can cite, as its handle CAP-<12 hex>.

NewerCaptureNotCitableWarning.title: NewerCaptureNotCitableWarning
NewerCaptureNotCitableWarning.description:
Contract evidence cited an older Capture: the newest cannot back a Claim.

``capture`` is that newest Capture. It is not committed as exact bytes, so no
Claim can map a source span onto it; the write cited the change's
``capture`` instead.

NextFinding.title: NextFinding
NextFinding.description: One more finding about the same underlying fact as the row that carries it.

NextHealth.title: NextHealth
NextHealth.description: One environment facet: its state, what it saw, and the repair if it needs one.

NextRebuildResult.title: NextRebuildResult
NextRebuildResult.description: Receipt for rebuilding the next worker's facts and rows from nothing.

NextRepairRequirement.title: NextRepairRequirement
NextRepairRequirement.description:
What running a withheld repair needs that this caller does not have.

The row stays in the queue; only its repair is withheld. ``because`` names
the gate: the permission ``tier`` the ``tool`` runs at, the MCP tool
``profile`` that advertises it, and/or ``authoring`` when this caller cannot
author here at all; ``authoring_refusal`` then carries whoami's code,
detail and repair. ``author``: only the proposal's author runs it.

NextStatus.title: NextStatus
NextStatus.description: The environment the queue was read in, beside the work rather than in it.

NoneClaimObject.title: NoneClaimObject
NoneClaimObject.description:
An inverse Claim's object: the unit its ClaimType's inverse names holds nothing.

``of`` names the unit within the slot: omitted for an inverse keyed by
``slot`` (the whole one-valued slot), the absent object itself for one keyed
by ``object``, and the key value (a literal in the key ClaimType's canonical
form) for one keyed by ``object_key``. Only a ClaimType that declares an
inverse admits one.

NoneNormalizer.title: NoneNormalizer
NoneNormalizer.description: The key part's value as it is (after its ClaimType's canonical form).

none.title: None
none.description: null, or the value (key) not held.

NoneValue.title: NoneValue
NoneValue.description: A none: the field holds nothing; needs a ClaimType inverse and its evidence.

NoteAuthoringPayload.title: NoteAuthoringPayload
NoteAuthoringPayload.description:
Link one workspace section ``about`` Subjects, or unlink it (contracts/notes.py).

``about`` is the note's complete Subject set after this change, sorted and
unique; empty retires the note. ``source`` is the section the writer's
adapter observed now (heading-path label required). Without one the change
names the ``note`` and only edits its links: they stay on the section bytes
the note already retains, so a deleted section can still be unlinked.

NumberType.title: NumberType
NumberType.description:
A number, integral or not. Its canonical encoding is an integer when the value
is integral and canonical decimal text otherwise, so ``1`` and ``1.0`` are equal
(:func:`canonical_number`). Bounds are canonical decimal strings, never floats.

claim.title: Claim
claim.description: A Claim ID (CLM-... or Claim:CLM-...); the daemon resolves its accepted version. An exact ClaimVersionReference object is accepted as the advanced form.

OperationSource.title: OperationSource
OperationSource.description:
Where an operation's code is.

``path`` is relative to the root of ``repository`` (or, for a local build
with no repository, to the provider's project directory). ``revision`` is
the full commit id the build was made from, and needs ``repository``.

OrientActivityCaptureErased.title: OrientActivityCaptureErased
OrientActivityCaptureErased.description:
A Capture's retained body was erased, by ``by``; ``ref`` is the Capture.

``at`` is when the erasure was recorded. ``unavailable`` marks a lost
erasure payload: the erasure is listed without the Capture it names.

OrientActivityCaptureLanded.title: OrientActivityCaptureLanded
OrientActivityCaptureLanded.description:
A run landed a Capture: ``capture`` is its handle, ``ref`` its ``Capture:<digest>``.

``contract`` names the CaptureContract it was taken under and
``logical_source`` the external source it read, when it read one. ``at``
is the landing run's evaluation instant, like its start and finish.
``unavailable`` marks a lost payload or an unreadable Capture: the landing
is listed by its run alone.

OrientActivityGenerationAccepted.title: OrientActivityGenerationAccepted
OrientActivityGenerationAccepted.description:
The ledger accepted a generation; the fields are an ``OrientGeneration``'s.

``ref`` (and ``proposal``) is the proposal whose admission accepted it, which
``get`` reads; genesis has neither. ``because`` is cut at 500 characters
(``because_truncated``). ``at`` is its acceptance time (the accepted
candidate's timestamp, or genesis's commit time); a candidate's timestamp
need not follow sequence, so the row is placed at the latest acceptance
time at or below it in sequence.

OrientActivityInboxDisposed.title: OrientActivityInboxDisposed
OrientActivityInboxDisposed.description:
An agent recorded a decision on an inbox item: acknowledged, dismissed or linked.

``at`` is when the decision was recorded.

OrientActivityInboxPosted.title: OrientActivityInboxPosted
OrientActivityInboxPosted.description:
A Line's run posted a new inbox item; ``ref`` is its id, which ``inbox get`` reads.

Only a new item is listed: a run posting the same payload again counts a
sighting on the item and is not new work. ``at`` is when the posting was
recorded: a run posts at its own evaluation instant.

OrientActivityLineStateChanged.title: OrientActivityLineStateChanged
OrientActivityLineStateChanged.description:
A Line's enablement moved from ``previous`` to ``state``; ``ref`` is the Line.

The states read as the ``lines`` section reads them: enabling makes a Line
``running``; a stop makes it ``stopped`` (``reason`` says why), or
``disabled`` when deliberately disabled or stopped with no reason (a
segment ending before its successor opens). ``previous`` is absent the
first time a Line is enabled. A daemon restart keeps a running Line
running and is not listed; ``stalled`` is read from due work, never
recorded, so it never appears here. ``at`` is when the enable or stop was
recorded.

OrientActivityOccurrenceDue.title: OrientActivityOccurrenceDue
OrientActivityOccurrenceDue.description:
A Trigger made one occurrence of a Line pending work, eligible from ``eligible_at``.

``trigger`` is the Trigger that derived it, absent for an explicit
evaluation that names none. ``ref`` is the Line. ``at`` is when the
evaluation that found it recorded it pending.

OrientActivityOccurrenceLapsed.title: OrientActivityOccurrenceLapsed
OrientActivityOccurrenceLapsed.description:
A pending timed tick lapsed as a new enablement opened; a retry still runs it.

``at`` is when the enablement that lapsed it was recorded.

OrientActivityRecordUnavailable.title: OrientActivityRecordUnavailable
OrientActivityRecordUnavailable.description:
A Line dispatch or inbox record whose payload is lost: what it recorded is unknown.

``at`` is the lost record's own instant. A lost inbox payload also stops
the inbox before the records after it (``cruxible.inbox.unavailable``),
so none of those are listed until it is restored.

OrientActivityRunFinished.title: OrientActivityRunFinished
OrientActivityRunFinished.description:
A Procedure run finished with ``status``, in the runs section's vocabulary.

``at`` is the run's evaluation instant, not the wall time it finished:
every record of a run carries that one instant (the executor's
deterministic clock), so a finish lists beside its start, above it.
``elapsed_us`` is how long the run took: the attempt's observed wall time
in microseconds, as its final record measured it (the run card's
``measured_wall_clock`` elapsed); ``at`` stays the evaluation instant.
It is absent when the final payload is lost or records none.
``unavailable`` marks a lost payload: a lost final payload reads as
``operational_failed``, as the runs section shows it.

OrientActivityRunStarted.title: OrientActivityRunStarted
OrientActivityRunStarted.description:
A Procedure run was admitted; ``ref`` (``ProcedureRun:<run>``) reads it.

``at`` is the run's evaluation instant, the ``started_at`` the runs
section shows. ``unavailable`` marks a run whose admission payload is
lost: the run is still listed, without its Procedure or Line.

OrientArtifactCounts.title: OrientArtifactCounts
OrientArtifactCounts.description:
How many of each family exist; each operational family is its own section.

``lines``, ``runbooks``, ``capture_contracts``, ``resolution_contracts`` and
``mandates`` count live accepted artifacts, ``capabilities`` the accepted
capability versions, ``captures`` the Captures accepted Claims cite,
and ``runs`` / ``running`` the Procedure runs admitted and still running.

OrientAttention.title: OrientAttention
OrientAttention.description:
What the ``next`` queue holds, and anything else the instance needs.

``next_items`` counts the queue's problems and ``top`` names the first of
them; ``setup_items`` counts its setup rows apart (choices the operator
owns, such as a Line accepted but not yet enabled), absent when none.
These count accepted state only: rows about the caller's workspace (its
floor, sources, projection blocks, vocabulary file) need the workspace
and appear in ``next``; orient reports the floor and the vocabulary file
as status beside this (``floor``, ``vocabulary_file``), as it always has.
``next_scope`` says so on every answer: ``next_items: 0`` is not an empty
``next`` queue.

OrientCapability.title: OrientCapability
OrientCapability.description:
One accepted capability version: a kind of call a Procedure slot names.

``capability`` is ``<name>@<version>``; ``get("Capability:<name>@<version>")``
reads it. ``in`` and ``out`` are its request and result Contracts
(``<name>@<version>``).

OrientClaimCounts.title: OrientClaimCounts
OrientClaimCounts.description:
Every accepted Claim by its status at the coordinate.

``accepted`` Claims answer their slot; ``conflicted`` ones are contenders
resolution left unresolved; ``overturned`` ones lost their slot to an
accepted rival; ``ineligible`` ones are not eligible to resolve under their
own ClaimType (a verdict other than supported, or erased evidence read
stale);
``retired`` ones were withdrawn. ``query(..., status=[...])`` lists the
non-live ones.

OrientContract.title: OrientContract
OrientContract.description:
One accepted Contract version: a data shape every edge is checked against.

``contract`` is ``<name>@<version>``; ``get("Contract:<name>@<version>")``
reads its fields. ``pins`` names the Contract versions it nests.

OrientEnablements.title: OrientEnablements
OrientEnablements.description:
The instance's enabled Lines as its Line consumer reports them, no daemon scope needed.

``running`` enablements are admitting their own due work; ``stalled`` ones have
due work older than the stall horizon; ``stopped`` ones stopped for any
reason but a deliberate disable. ``needs_attention`` names up to three
stalled or stopped Lines (``Line:<name> stopped (<reason>)``), each a
``get`` reference.

OrientEvidenceCounts.title: OrientEvidenceCounts
OrientEvidenceCounts.description:
How the live Claims of one ClaimType are backed (W8).

``admitted``: they cite a Capture admitted under the ClaimType's evidence
rule (independent evidence, not the author's own words). ``own_word``: no
captured evidence, and the type's rule permits a Claim on its own words.
``unmet``: the type requires captured evidence and none was admitted.

OrientFloor.title: OrientFloor
OrientFloor.description:
The workspace's greppable floor: the coordinate it is at, and how stale.

Only a client that sees the workspace (CLI, MCP, SDK) fills this in, from
the floor's own manifest; a daemon answer never carries it.
``generations_behind`` counts accepted generations from the floor to this
answer's coordinate; ``None`` when the floor predates generation stamps.

OrientGeneration.title: OrientGeneration
OrientGeneration.description:
One accepted generation, newest first: what accepted it and how much it changed.

``changeset_digest`` names the change-set record; ``proposal`` is the
proposal whose admission it accepted (``get <proposal>`` reads its card and
changes), ``proposer`` the actor bound to it, and ``approvals`` the
approving signers in record order. ``because`` is that admission's
rationale, cut at 500 characters (``because_truncated``). ``members``
counts the change set's members; ``since(generation=sequence-1,
at=<this generation>)`` lists them. Genesis (sequence 0) carries only its
sequence, git oid and time. ``proposed_at`` is when the change set was
proposed (its candidate's timestamp); rows are ordered by ``sequence``, and
the instant of acceptance is not recorded. Pass ``sequence`` or ``git_oid``
as ``at`` to read state as this generation left it.

OrientGraph.title: OrientGraph
OrientGraph.description:
One page of the Subject graph: live Subjects, then live Subject-valued Claims.

A page holds up to ``limit`` rows: nodes first (by kind, then Subject),
and once the nodes are done, edges (by target, then Claim). Follow
``next_cursor`` while ``truncated``; every page reads at the first page's
coordinate.

OrientGraphEdge.title: OrientGraphEdge
OrientGraphEdge.description:
One live Claim whose object is a Subject: ``source`` --predicate--> ``target``.

``claim`` is the Claim's id (``get`` reads it); ``source`` and ``target``
are ``kind/id`` refs. A relation is stored once, on its source.

OrientGraphNode.title: OrientGraphNode
OrientGraphNode.description: One live Subject: ``subject`` is its ``kind/id`` ref, which ``get`` reads.

OrientGraphTotals.title: OrientGraphTotals
OrientGraphTotals.description:
The whole graph's size at the coordinate, on every page.

``subjects`` is the live Subject count, read from the per-kind counters
the projection maintains (never a recount).

OrientKindDetail.title: OrientKindDetail
OrientKindDetail.description:
One kind in full, with a few Subject IDs to read next.

``incoming`` names, in full, the Subject-valued predicates of other kinds
whose values may name this kind's Subjects: the reverse follows a ``query``
on this kind can take (``follow`` with ``direction: "reverse"``). It is
omitted when nothing points at the kind.

OrientKindEnd.title: OrientKindEnd
OrientKindEnd.description: One Subject-valued key part of a pair kind: its key ClaimType and the end's kind.

OrientKindSummary.title: OrientKindSummary
OrientKindSummary.description:
One Subject kind in the default map: its live Subjects and first fields.

``fields`` names its first predicates by short name (byte order), at most
``ORIENT_KIND_FIELDS``; ``more_fields`` counts the rest. ``identity`` is
as on ``OrientKind``. ``orient(kind=...)`` reads every predicate in full.

OrientMandate.title: OrientMandate
OrientMandate.description:
One mandate row: its grant and state, the ClaimTypes a settle grant covers,
its condition query's ref, the Subject kinds it may create, and ``suspended``
when its kill switch is on. ``line`` is the Line it grants. ``get`` reads the
rest.

OrientOperation.title: OrientOperation
OrientOperation.description:
One operation a live provider build serves: what a Line can bind a slot to.

``description`` is the provider's own words for it; ``serves`` names the
capabilities it declares; ``source`` is where its code is (``path`` in
``repository`` at ``revision``, when the build names them). ``input`` and
``output`` name its own Contracts (``name@N``), copies the build carries.
``build`` is the exact build (``Provider:<name>/<build key>``); a Line
binding names it as ``<build>#<operation>``. ``refusals`` lists the typed
refusal codes it may return, and ``absorbable`` those a Line rule with
``on_unavailable: omit`` may absorb. ``may_truncate``: it may return a
truncated listing. ``get("Provider:<build>")`` reads the whole build.

OrientPin.title: OrientPin
OrientPin.description:
One dependency of a live definition, identified by source, field and target.

``current`` says whether the reference resolves to a live target.
Read in reverse, the rows name who
uses a contract, a ClaimType or a Procedure: the Procedures that capture
under a contract (role ``capture-contract``), the Lines on a Procedure,
the mandates that settle a ClaimType.

OrientPredicate.title: OrientPredicate
OrientPredicate.description:
One predicate of a kind: compact by default, in full under ``orient(kind=...)``.

``name`` is the short name a query field uses against this kind; ``predicate``
is the full ClaimType predicate. ``type`` is the native Contract type spelling,
including enum members and
``subject<K1 | K2>`` for a Subject-valued predicate.
``evidence`` names the CaptureContracts the ClaimType admits; a digest that
names no accepted contract shows as ``unresolved:<short digest>``.
``None`` (omitted on the wire) inherits the kind's evidence set; an empty
tuple (``[]`` on the wire) explicitly admits no contracts. Standalone
descriptors always carry an explicit set.

``description`` is the ClaimType's (v7) description: its first sentence, at
most 160 characters, in a compact descriptor; all of it in full.
``evidence_requirement`` appears only when it is not ``self`` (``none``: the
Claim's own origin supports it; ``captured``: a Capture under a declared
contract is required). A full descriptor also carries each described enum
member, the role a write defaults to, and ``revision_evidence``: what a
statement-changing revision keeps.
A full descriptor also names how the ClaimType settles rival Claims
(``contention``), its format version (``format``: 10 for
``cruxible-claim-type-v11``), its accepted ``revision`` and its ledger
``path``, which a kit's drifted paths name. Under ``orient(kind=K)`` a
descriptor counts the kind's ``live_claims`` of the predicate and
``subjects_with_value``: its live Subjects with at least one, both read
from counters Claim writes maintain. A full descriptor's
``evidence_counts`` splits the ClaimType's live Claims (every kind) by how
they are backed: admitted captured evidence, own words, or unmet.
``kit`` (claim_types section only) is the installed kit that owns the
ClaimType: its receipt records the definition. Absent when no kit owns it.

OrientQuery.title: OrientQuery
OrientQuery.description: One named QueryDefinition; params read ``name: type`` with ``?`` when optional.

OrientResult.title: OrientResult
OrientResult.description:
One orient answer; which parts are present depends on the request.

- no ``kind``/``section``: ``you``, ``kinds`` (paged by ``limit``/``cursor``),
  ``artifacts``, ``queries`` and ``attention``;
- ``kind``: ``kind_detail``;
- ``section``: that section's rows (``documents``, ``procedures``,
  ``claim_types``, ``subject_kinds``, ``queries``, ``operations``, or an
  operational family:
  ``runs``, ``running``, ``lines``, ``runbooks``, ``captures``,
  ``capture_contracts``,
  ``predictions``, ``mandates``), the logical sources runs landed
  Captures from (``sources``), the principal registry (``principals``),
  the governed policies in force (``policies``), the accepted generations
  newest first (``generations``), the Subject graph (``graph``), the
  pins between live definitions (``pins``) or what just happened, newest
  first (``activity``), paged.
  The default map counts the operational families under ``artifacts`` and
  never inlines their rows.

``next`` is rendered for the requesting surface.

OrientRunbook.title: OrientRunbook
OrientRunbook.description: One Runbook row: its steps, Triggers aimed at it, and its latest run (read live).

OrientSource.title: OrientSource
OrientSource.description:
One logical source runs have landed Captures from, cited or not.

``landings`` counts its landings (the ``capture_landed`` events the
activity feed lists), ``latest`` is the most recent, and ``contracts`` the
contract versions they were landed under, each with its count.

OrientSourceContract.title: OrientSourceContract
OrientSourceContract.description:
One CaptureContract version a logical source's landed Captures are under.

``version`` counts that contract's accepted versions at the current head; it
is absent when the digest names no accepted version there (``contract``
then reads ``unresolved:<digest>``).

OrientSourceLanding.title: OrientSourceLanding
OrientSourceLanding.description:
A logical source's latest landing: the run that landed it and the Capture it landed.

``landed_at`` is the landing record's instant, ``run`` and ``line`` the run
that recorded it (``line`` absent for a direct run). ``capture`` is the
Capture's handle and ``ref`` its ``Capture:<digest>``; ``observed_at`` and
``size`` come from its envelope; ``status``, ``status_detail`` and
``erased`` say, as the Capture card does, whether the store can still
produce it. ``unavailable`` marks a landing whose payload or envelope can
no longer be read: the landing is listed by its run alone.

OrientSubjectKind.title: OrientSubjectKind
OrientSubjectKind.description:
One live SubjectKind: how core names a new Subject of the kind.

``rule`` is ``keys`` (named by its key ClaimTypes, in key order, ``unique``
or ``hint``) or ``minted`` (core mints the id). A kind with no live
SubjectKind has no row: no new Subject of it can be created. ``ends``
lists a pair kind's Subject-valued key parts, in key order: a pair kind is
keyed by its ends. ``kit`` is the installed kit that owns the SubjectKind,
absent when no kit owns it.

OrientVocabularyFile.title: OrientVocabularyFile
OrientVocabularyFile.description:
The workspace's vocabulary file against this answer's coordinate.

Only a client that sees the workspace (CLI, MCP, SDK) asks for it, naming the
generation the file's header was exported at; the daemon counts the
ClaimTypes and SubjectKinds accepted since. ``invalid``: the header cannot be
read, or names an export this instance does not hold.

OrientWorkspaceFiles.title: OrientWorkspaceFiles
OrientWorkspaceFiles.description:
The workspace's catalogued files (files.yaml), by path: what notes and
section citations point into, and what ``cruxible section FILE#Heading`` reads.

Only a client that sees the workspace (CLI, MCP, SDK) fills this in, on the
default map; a daemon answer never carries it. ``paths`` are the first
``ORIENT_WORKSPACE_FILES`` in byte order; ``total`` counts them all.

OrientYou.title: OrientYou
OrientYou.description: The caller as the daemon resolved it, and whether it can author.

OriginatingLine.title: OriginatingLine
OriginatingLine.description: The root Line and exact accepted version responsible for a proposal.

Pep503Normalizer.title: Pep503Normalizer
Pep503Normalizer.description: A Python package name in its PEP 503 normal form.

PresentationPolicy.title: PresentationPolicy
PresentationPolicy.description: Current local-only presentation policy; V1 remains readable.

PresentationPolicyV1.title: PresentationPolicyV1
PresentationPolicyV1.description: Local-only suppression policy for presentation diagnostics.

PrincipalRecord.title: PrincipalRecord
PrincipalRecord.description: One public principal record stored in the signed genesis tree.

PriorRefusalCoverage.title: PriorRefusalCoverage
PriorRefusalCoverage.description:
How far earlier retirements were indexed when receipts were read.

Present only while the index is catching up: receipts then reflect
retirements accepted through ``indexed_through_generation`` of
``accepted_generation``. Rejections are always current.

PriorRefusalReceipt.title: PriorRefusalReceipt
PriorRefusalReceipt.description:
An earlier refusal of the same statement on the same evidence, as recorded.

``claim_retired``: ``claim_id`` was retired by ``decided_by`` at ``decided_at``
with ``reason_code`` (its retirement reason, when attributed) and the
retiring change's ``rationale``; ``proposal_id`` is that change's proposal
when known. ``proposal_rejected``: a reviewer, ``decided_by``, rejected
``proposal_id`` (which proposed ``claim_id``) at ``decided_at``, giving
``rationale``; a rejection records no reason code. ``producer`` is the
Procedure the prior Claim named, when it named one. Nothing here is a
verdict on the new Claim.

ProcedureAdmissionMaterialMember.title: ProcedureAdmissionMaterialMember
ProcedureAdmissionMaterialMember.description:
One admission-material retention decision.

``retain_until`` reads VALIDITY WINDOW.

ProcedureArtifact.title: ProcedureArtifact
ProcedureArtifact.description:
The one Procedure envelope: one named graph.

Every dependency the graph names -- its input, output and parameter
Contracts included, which are governed Contracts -- resolves at the
accepted coordinate; the envelope itself pins nothing and carries no
Contracts. Acquisition rules are not the Procedure's:
its Line declares them per capture output (``<alias>.<field>``).

ProcedureAuthoringPayload.title: ProcedureAuthoringPayload
ProcedureAuthoringPayload.description:
A lowered Procedure: its stored graph and the boundary Contracts core co-proposes.

``generated`` holds the inline fields of each boundary (``input``,
``output``, ``params``) the spec declared inline; lowering co-proposes the
governed Contract ``<procedure>.<role>@N`` for each, versioned with the
Procedure (a successor reuses version N when its fields are unchanged), and
points the definition at it. A boundary the spec names (``name@N``) is not
here. Acquisition rules are not the Procedure's: its Line declares them.

message.const: A Procedure collection exceeded its declared item bound.
message.title: Message
message.default: A Procedure collection exceeded its declared item bound.

ProcedureChildInvocation.title: ProcedureChildInvocation
ProcedureChildInvocation.description: A completed child occurrence, navigable by run ID without copying digests.

ProcedureDefinition.title: ProcedureDefinition
ProcedureDefinition.description:
The one Procedure graph: explicit value joins and typed return paths.

Every dependency field names a governed identity; an execution plan
resolves each to its exact pin at the run's accepted coordinate.
``slots`` names, for each provider-calling node, the capability it needs
(``{capability, may_truncate}``; its request and result Contracts and
effect come from that capability). The Procedure never names a provider;
a Line binds every slot to one exact build and operation serving that
capability when it is accepted.

ProcedureEgressCaptureEvidence.title: ProcedureEgressCaptureEvidence
ProcedureEgressCaptureEvidence.description: Procedure producer-receipt evidence with no Provider-only fields.

ProcedureFailureCause.title: ProcedureFailureCause
ProcedureFailureCause.description:
What the Provider said when its invocation failed for an operational reason.

Projected from the run's own completion, never re-derived: ``provider_code``
is the Provider outcome's code, ``kind`` its error kind when the runtime
names one (a transport error and an HTTP status differ here), and
``message`` the Provider's message with URL userinfo stripped.

ProcedureInput.title: ProcedureInput
ProcedureInput.description:
A Procedure, authored in the one typed form: a :class:`ProcedureSpec`.

The stored Procedure graph is produced by lowering the spec; a graph is
never authored directly, and the retired Python source request is refused
(``procedure_authoring_form_retired``).

ProcedureLimits.title: ProcedureLimits
ProcedureLimits.description: A Procedure's hard caps as authored (lowered to ``ProcedureHardCaps``).

ProcedureMandateAuthoringPayload.title: ProcedureMandateAuthoringPayload
ProcedureMandateAuthoringPayload.description:
Decision-only grant input; lowering owns every exact digest it pins.

The validity window is exactly one of ``expires_at`` or ``expires`` (a
span such as ``90d``); ``valid_from`` omitted is the intent's timestamp.
Lowering stores both as concrete UTC instants.

valid_from.title: Valid From
valid_from.description: Give exactly one of expires_at (an instant) or expires (a span: 36h, 90d, 12w, 1y, P90D). valid_from defaults to the intent's time; expires counts from valid_from.

include_derived.title: Include Derived
include_derived.description: scope: observations only: also settle values on basis derived.

subject_creation.title: Subject Creation
subject_creation.description: Settle grants only: Subject kinds a run may create by key; their new Subjects and key Claims settle with the change. A propose grant names subjects/<kind> in its namespace instead.

ProcedureMandateInput.title: ProcedureMandateInput
ProcedureMandateInput.description:
A propose grant, or a settle grant with its Claim scope and condition query.

``line_name`` names the Line the grant authorizes (accepted, or defined in
the same set); lowering pins its exact digest, so changing the Line's
Procedure version, parameters or bindings renews the grant. ``grants`` is
the verb the mandate delegates. A settle grant names the ClaimTypes (by
predicate), per change kind the evidence bases that settle, an optional
``value: {from, to}`` for enum and bool ClaimTypes, and an optional accepted
condition query (which may bind ``$target.value`` and ``$target.before``);
lowering pins every exact digest. ``subjects: expected`` limits the grant
to Subjects the Line's claims templates fence with ``within``.

``scope: observations`` is one settle grant over the observations the Line
writes: lowering pins every ClaimType of the Procedure's claims templates
(each must permit only the observation role), with creates and revises on
``extracted`` and ``measured`` (plus ``derived`` with ``include_derived``)
and the absence changes its ``when_absent`` templates make; the namespace
defaults to ``claims``.

ProcedureMeasureRequest.title: ProcedureMeasureRequest
ProcedureMeasureRequest.description:
Evaluate the due measurements of one accepted Procedure, optionally for one run.

``evaluation_time`` is the explicit OBSERVATION INSTANT; ``at`` is the
OBSERVATION COORDINATE. Both default to the daemon's current view when
omitted. ``run_id`` names the real run whose grain a reading should
credit; without it only the contract-level resolution is produced.

ProcedureMeasurementContractStatus.title: ProcedureMeasurementContractStatus
ProcedureMeasurementContractStatus.description: Read-only standing of one activation at the inspection instant.

ProcedureMeasurementDeclaration.title: ProcedureMeasurementDeclaration
ProcedureMeasurementDeclaration.description: One digest-covered declaration from which PC-E1 may derive activation.

ProcedureMeasurementEligibility.title: ProcedureMeasurementEligibility
ProcedureMeasurementEligibility.description:
The window the producer honours, and where this evaluation stood in it.

``activated_at`` reads the signed acceptance instant of the declaring
generation; ``check_at`` and ``expires_at`` are that instant plus the
declaration's ``check_after`` and ``expires_after``. The producer evaluates
only inside ``[check_at, expires_at)``: before it the measurement is
pending, at or after ``expires_at`` it is expired, and neither writes a
resolution. The frozen resolution law is narrower than this producer rule
and is left exactly as it was.

ProcedureMeasurementExpectation.title: ProcedureMeasurementExpectation
ProcedureMeasurementExpectation.description: Closed point-in-time count and property-equality expectation.

ProcedureMeasurementResolutionSummary.title: ProcedureMeasurementResolutionSummary
ProcedureMeasurementResolutionSummary.description: The standing resolution for one activation, with its retrievable record.

ProcedureMeasurementReviewTrigger.title: ProcedureMeasurementReviewTrigger
ProcedureMeasurementReviewTrigger.description: A deterministic threshold that can later request calibration review.

ProcedureMeasurementRow.title: ProcedureMeasurementRow
ProcedureMeasurementRow.description: One declared measurement's outcome for this evaluation request.

ProcedureMeasurementSituationShape.title: ProcedureMeasurementSituationShape
ProcedureMeasurementSituationShape.description: Coarse reproducible context, excluding task IDs and answer content.

ProcedureNodeRefusal.title: ProcedureNodeRefusal
ProcedureNodeRefusal.description:
One node's refusal.

``detail_code`` carries an authored code: for ``guard_refused`` the guard's,
for ``operation_refused`` the refusal code the bound provider operation
declares (its own vocabulary, with ``details`` its declared detail).

ProcedureNodeSupport.title: ProcedureNodeSupport
ProcedureNodeSupport.description: One node the direct run lane does not execute, and where it can run.

ProcedureProviderBinding.title: ProcedureProviderBinding
ProcedureProviderBinding.description:
What one slotted node binds at admission: its slot's exact build and operation.

The binding is the Line's (or, for a direct run, the request's ephemeral
spec), never chosen at run time. ``capability`` is the slot's capability
pin and ``fit`` how the operation fit it at admission; ``fit`` is omitted
only for a capability core's builtin serves (bound by name).

ProcedureReadiness.title: ProcedureReadiness
ProcedureReadiness.description: How one accepted Procedure can run, with its exact artifact (SDK internal read).

ProcedureReadingSummary.title: ProcedureReadingSummary
ProcedureReadingSummary.description: One retained exact-grain reading and the run it credits.

ProcedureReadingsRequest.title: ProcedureReadingsRequest
ProcedureReadingsRequest.description: Bounded, paginated inspection of retained readings. Never writes.

ProcedureRunAttributionWithheld.title: ProcedureRunAttributionWithheld
ProcedureRunAttributionWithheld.description:
A run's attribution with its actor withheld from this reader.

An armed run acts as its arming credential's principal. A reader who may
not see that credential -- not an admin, not the credential itself, and
not another credential bound to the same principal -- reads everything but
the actor, the same rule the Line and run cards apply to ``armed_by``.

ProcedureRunBudget.title: ProcedureRunBudget
ProcedureRunBudget.description: The one budget grammar: declared bounds and observed high-water values.

ProcedureRunBudgetDeclared.title: ProcedureRunBudgetDeclared
ProcedureRunBudgetDeclared.description:
The run's declared budget: what it admitted, and the caps in force.

``provider_output_bytes_cap`` is present exactly for a run that planned
Provider occurrences.

ProcedureRunReceipt.title: ProcedureRunReceipt
ProcedureRunReceipt.description:
The one public run receipt, for every run lane.

A direct run (``invocation_origin="actor"``) names no Line coordinate; a
Line run names its LineSpec, occurrence, deployment, acquisition policy,
sensitivity and mandate coordinates. A run that planned Provider
occurrences names its acquisition plan, selection decision and Provider
bindings, its durable invocation receipts and its Source Capture
associations; a pure run names none of them.

``bound_coordinate.generation``, ``head_at_admission.generation`` and the
``first_sequence``/``last_sequence`` journal range read SETTLEMENT ORDER.
``evaluation_time``, ``occurrence_evaluation_time`` and
``attribution.recorded_time`` read EVALUATION INSTANT. Every
``admission_material_manifest.members[].retain_until`` and Provider budget
or duration field reads VALIDITY WINDOW.

ProcedureRunReceiptWithheld.title: ProcedureRunReceiptWithheld
ProcedureRunReceiptWithheld.description:
A run receipt withheld from this reader: it carries the arming credential's actor.

``receipt_digest`` beside it still names the exact receipt.

bindings.title: Bindings
bindings.description: Slot -> 'provider[/build][#operation]'; an invoked child's slot is '<invoke node>.<slot>'. Omitted slots are fitted when the run is admitted.

acquisition.title: Acquisition
acquisition.description: Per capture output <alias>.<field> (an invoked child's: <invoke node path>.<alias>.<field>): {max_age, on_unavailable, ...}. The direct run's ephemeral Line spec carries them; one left out runs under the core default.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: The run's Procedure parameter values (its ephemeral Line spec's), over the Procedure's parameter_defaults; checked against its params Contract.

ProcedureSourceCaptureAssociation.title: ProcedureSourceCaptureAssociation
ProcedureSourceCaptureAssociation.description: One capture field of one Provider occurrence, and the Capture it produced.

ProcedureSourceObservation.title: ProcedureSourceObservation
ProcedureSourceObservation.description:
What one admitted Source occurrence really observed, per run.

Additive and optional: a run with no Source occurrence carries none. The
read receipt is the daemon's attestation of the exact bytes it read; the
capture digest names the Capture those bytes became. Full lineage from a
Claim back to this run is a later contract, not this field.

input.title: Input
input.description: Input fields (Contract field spellings); core co-proposes the governed <procedure>.input@N Contract. Or name one with input_contract.

params.title: Params
params.description: Parameter fields a Line supplies (Contract field spellings); core co-proposes the governed <procedure>.params@N Contract. A field may state its default inline as {type, default}.

parameter_defaults.title: Parameter Defaults
parameter_defaults.description: Each parameter's default by name; a Line's value overrides it. The params Contract stays shape-only, and each default must fit its field.

hard_caps.description: The most any run of this Procedure may use. The operating budget is the Line's (a direct run's ephemeral Line spec), within these caps.

slots.title: Slots
slots.description: Each slot's capability, {capability: name@N} (and may_truncate); a Line binds it to an operation that serves and fits it.

ProcedureTarget.title: ProcedureTarget
ProcedureTarget.description:
Fan-out step: run each live Line of this Procedure, in Line-name order.

The Lines are read at the head when the step is reached. A Line that takes
an event is left out (``cruxible.runbook.line_takes_event``); with no Line
left the step is skipped (``cruxible.runbook.no_lines_bound``). Each Line
runs as a Line step does (``LineTarget``): in a Trigger-fired run a Line not
enabled stops the Runbook with ``not_enabled``, as a Line step's would; a
manual run runs it under the caller's authority.

ProcedureTerminalEgress.title: ProcedureTerminalEgress
ProcedureTerminalEgress.description:
What one terminal node of a run did, reconstructed from its journal.

Additive and optional: a run with no terminal carries none. A delivered
`claims` names the proposal and the exact candidate it produced,
so a manager can retrieve, review and activate that candidate through the
existing proposal doors; producing it never activates it. A refused or
failed egress names the code the run refused with, so the run reads as the
reason it stopped rather than as a bare failure.

ProcedureTerminalEgressChild.title: ProcedureTerminalEgressChild
ProcedureTerminalEgressChild.description: One fanout child of a terminal, and the handle its sink produced for it.

ProjectNode.title: ProjectNode
ProjectNode.description:
A typed record: ``fields`` resolved from the run, or an exact ``literal``.

A ``literal`` record is data: dollar-prefixed strings in it are never
references. A ``leaf`` project is a successful terminal that returns its
own value, so each branch may return its own exact result.

ProjectStep.title: ProjectStep
ProjectStep.description:
A typed record: ``fields`` resolved from the run, or an exact ``literal``.

A ``literal`` is data: nothing in it is a reference. ``leaf: true`` makes
the record this branch's own return value (a leaf has no successor).

ProjectionAdvisoryPolicy.title: ProjectionAdvisoryPolicy
ProjectionAdvisoryPolicy.description: Per-artifact-kind switches for local projection advisories.

ProjectionArtifactBacking.title: ProjectionArtifactBacking
ProjectionArtifactBacking.description: A governed vocabulary or entity artifact pinned by exact digest.

ProjectionBlockStampV1.title: ProjectionBlockStampV1
ProjectionBlockStampV1.description: Frozen encoding for retained declarations; newly authored stamps use V2.

ProjectionCoverageBinding.title: ProjectionCoverageBinding
ProjectionCoverageBinding.description: One client-observed mapping from governed identity to local projection path.

ProjectionCoverageObservation.title: ProjectionCoverageObservation
ProjectionCoverageObservation.description: Bounded local projection evidence at one exact accepted coordinate.

ProjectionEvidence.title: ProjectionEvidence
ProjectionEvidence.description: Whether one bounded workspace projection observation informed review.

ProjectionResolvedParameterBinding.title: ProjectionResolvedParameterBinding
ProjectionResolvedParameterBinding.description: The exact existing query-parameter-binding wire spelling, shared by both sides.

ProposalItemReason.title: ProposalItemReason
ProposalItemReason.description:
One Procedure terminal item's own reason, kept with the member it explains.

A ``claims`` or ``claims`` item states why in its
``rationale``; the change set's rationale names only the run and the item
count, and each item's reason is recorded here, keyed by the immutable
Procedure operation (``operation``: the terminal's admission binding and
node, the identity its core creation records use) and the path of the
Claim (or Subject) it lowered into. A proposal reads them only through its
own ``ProposalItemReasonLink``, never through its (reusable) ref. It is
provenance, not evidence: the Claim's Captures are unchanged.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

change_set_record_bytes_per_member.title: Change Set Record Bytes Per Member

ProposalReceiveLimits.title: ProposalReceiveLimits
ProposalReceiveLimits.description:
Every bound proposal receive enforces before a single member is parsed.

The file-count and aggregate-byte ceilings track the adoption posture of
`TreeReadLimits`: a proposal carries the whole candidate tree, so a receive
ceiling below the tree-read ceiling would make a legally accepted instance
unproposable. The other three keep receive itself bounded no matter how
large the accepted tree has grown -- how many members one submission may
change, how large a single member may be, and how deep a member path may
nest -- so an oversized submission is refused on cheap metadata instead of
after parsing.

The last two are ADVERTISEMENTS rather than receive gates, and they are here
because this is the object a caller reads to learn what a submission may
carry. The ledger writes its record OF a change set as one blob, measured
against the per-blob ceiling; a set that satisfies every receive bound above
could once still exceed it, which was discovered only at activation, after
the compile. Advertising the ceiling and the per-entry cost next to the
member budget lets a caller compute the member count that fits before
authoring anything.

They are no longer a SECOND budget. At the 4 MiB ceiling this shipped with,
only 372 entries fit -- far below `max_changed_members` -- so the two numbers
stood side by side bounding different things, one what receive accepts and
one what the ledger can record. The per-blob ceiling is now 64 MiB and they
are ONE number: 5,000 entries at 11,264 bytes each project to 56,320,000
bytes, about 53.7 MiB, so the advertised member budget fits under the record
ceiling with room left, and `max_change_set_members` (5,957 at the defaults)
is a derived reading of the same budget rather than a competing one.

What both bound is RECORD ENTRIES, not authored members: the record holds one
entry per path the set lowers to, and a member may lower to several -- a
ClaimType succession writes one per dependent it dispositions, a retirement
one per Claim in its closure. `max_change_set_members` is therefore the
entry budget, and a set of that many 1:1 members is the largest set it
names exactly.

``in`` and ``out`` are Contract refs (``name@N``). ``declared_endpoints``
and ``requires_extras`` are the manifest row of the operation's entrypoint.

ReviewWorkspaceObservation.title: ReviewWorkspaceObservation
ReviewWorkspaceObservation.description: Review-scoped subset of local projection facts; no daemon path access.

RunCompleteness.title: RunCompleteness
RunCompleteness.description:
A run's completeness summary: present when incomplete or when expect met ``within``.

``complete`` is derived: false exactly when a reason, downgrade or skipped
write was recorded. ``expect_outside_within`` counts expected Subjects
outside the step's ``within`` (never retired or inverted).

RunCounts.title: RunCounts
RunCounts.description:
What one Line run did, in counts: the line a reader checks before "succeeded".

``status`` says the run finished; this says what it achieved. ``written``
counts new, revising and inverse Claims across the run's claims terminals;
``settled`` and ``proposed`` split them by how each terminal delivered
(``proposed`` includes a change still waiting on the Line's open proposal).
``unchanged`` counts re-observed and no-op restatements (a re-observation
whose record was refused included), ``retired`` the
retirements. ``refused`` counts the items not written (every finding but
an incomplete source), with ``top_refusals`` naming the most frequent codes
among the findings the run kept. ``inbox`` counts the items this run posted
to its Line's inbox; when the inbox could not be read it is the count the
run's journaled ``post_inbox`` summaries prove, or ``None`` when they prove
none (findings routed to the inbox are not journaled). It splits into
``inbox_new``, the postings that made a new item, and ``inbox_seen_again``,
the re-sightings of an item already there (which keep its status and
decision); both are ``None`` when the split is unknown (the inbox could
not be read, or the counts were recorded before the split existed).
``inbox_unposted`` counts the items an inbox cap left out of this run's
posts. ``complete`` is false when the run recorded incompleteness, with
``incomplete_reasons`` naming each node and kind. ``needs_attention`` is
true when the run was incomplete, refused an item, posted a new inbox item,
left items out under an inbox cap (they may be new: nothing posted them),
or posted to the inbox without a known split: an unreadable count never
reads as nothing new. A run whose posts were all re-sightings does not
need attention for them.

RunRefusalCount.title: RunRefusalCount
RunRefusalCount.description:
One refusal code and how many of the run's findings carried it.

``code`` is the finding kind, with its problem when it names one
(``extract_refused.value_invalid``).

RunRow.title: RunRow
RunRow.description: One Procedure run as a list row, newest admission first; ``status`` never orders.

RunbookAuthoringPayload.title: RunbookAuthoringPayload
RunbookAuthoringPayload.description:
One Runbook decision (D-R36): an ordered list of Lines, Procedures and internal actions.

No branching, no parameters of its own and no new action kinds: each Line
step runs as that Line's manual occurrence, on its own parameters and
authority; a Procedure step runs every live Line of that Procedure, in
Line-name order. ``retire`` retires the accepted Runbook (``steps`` then unused).

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: In run order: {line: <Line name>}, {procedure: <Procedure name>} or {action: <internal action>}.

RunbookInput.title: RunbookInput
RunbookInput.description:
An ordered list of Lines and internal actions, run in order (D-R36).

Each step names exactly one accepted Line (``line``) or registered internal
action (``action``). No branching, no parameters of its own: a Line step runs
as that Line's manual occurrence, on its own parameters, budgets and authority.
A run stops at the first step that fails or whose writes go to review.
``retire`` retires the accepted Runbook.

RunbookOrderProblem.title: RunbookOrderProblem
RunbookOrderProblem.description: A read the order cannot serve: reported, never fixed.

RunbookPreview.title: RunbookPreview
RunbookPreview.description:
A static composed graph of one Runbook, from accepted definitions only.

It never executes a step, reads no Claims, Captures or journals, and
predicts no outcome: no record counts, no value changes, no whether a
proposal happens. It says what each step can do, and what each step's run
needs from outside: the one thing it checks beyond definitions is whether
each workspace file a step reads is there (a stat; no byte is read).

RunbookPreviewAuthority.title: RunbookPreviewAuthority
RunbookPreviewAuthority.description:
What the step's Line may do with its writes, from its Mandate scope.

Static: a write is shown as settling only when every restriction of the
grant can be proven from definitions (ClaimType, change kind, the value's
evidence basis, no value or Subject restriction). Anything that cannot be
proven is listed in ``review_gaps`` and may go to review.

RunbookPreviewCall.title: RunbookPreviewCall
RunbookPreviewCall.description:
One provider call: its slot's capability, the signature derived from it, and the
binding the Line pins.

RunbookPreviewCascade.title: RunbookPreviewCascade
RunbookPreviewCascade.description: A Trigger the step's writes can set off, during or after the run.

RunbookPreviewInput.title: RunbookPreviewInput
RunbookPreviewInput.description:
One input the step's run takes from outside accepted state, as declared.

``location`` is the path, glob or URL, resolved from the Line's parameters
(null when the run computes it). ``description`` is the params Contract
field's description for ``parameter``, as the author wrote it (null when
none is written). ``state`` is reported for a workspace file only.

RunbookPreviewInputLimits.title: RunbookPreviewInputLimits
RunbookPreviewInputLimits.description: The limits the input's CaptureContract declares (and a glob's file cap).

RunbookPreviewRead.title: RunbookPreviewRead
RunbookPreviewRead.description: One read a step's Procedure declares, and the vocabulary behind it.

RunbookPreviewWrite.title: RunbookPreviewWrite
RunbookPreviewWrite.description: One claims node a step's Procedure declares: the ClaimTypes it can write.

RunbookRunResult.title: RunbookRunResult
RunbookRunResult.description: One run of a Runbook: every step's outcome, in order, and why it stopped.

RunbookSettleChange.title: RunbookSettleChange
RunbookSettleChange.description: One change kind a settle grant covers, and the evidence bases it settles on.

RunbookSettleScope.title: RunbookSettleScope
RunbookSettleScope.description: One ClaimType a settle grant covers, with every restriction the grant states.

anyOf.description: A registered internal action: floor.refresh, evidence.sweep, prediction.anchor_retry.

RunbookStepAuthoring.title: RunbookStepAuthoring
RunbookStepAuthoring.description: One Runbook step: exactly one of an accepted Line, a registered action, or a Procedure.

RunbookStepOutcome.title: RunbookStepOutcome
RunbookStepOutcome.description: What one step did: its Line run (or action fire) and how it stood.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

RuntimeCredentialMintStatement.title: RuntimeCredentialMintStatement
RuntimeCredentialMintStatement.description: Exactly the bytes a principal signs to consent to one credential.

RuntimeCredentialPrincipalProof.title: RuntimeCredentialPrincipalProof
RuntimeCredentialPrincipalProof.description: A mint statement and the principal's Ed25519 signature over it.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: true: run every check up to the commit and write nothing, answering with a would_* status; false: commit. Omitted: this operation's default (a change derived across several artifacts, or one that cannot be undone, previews).

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate a preview answered with: its git oid, or for a change to operational state its state digest (either may be shortened to a unique prefix of 12+ hex characters). A commit carrying it refuses cruxible.preview.state_moved if that state moved since. Required to commit a change that cannot be undone.

observation.description: Filled by the client that read the section; leave it out.

SectionEvidence.title: SectionEvidence
SectionEvidence.description:
Cite a section's own body; the client observes it after this write's edits.

Authored prose may be used as the writer's own words, with a locating copy.
ClaimType admission still names fetched contracts; no authored-byte tracking
or new provenance authority is implied by ``own_words``.

SectionSelector.title: SectionSelector
SectionSelector.description: A heading-path label; byte commitments, never this label, decide drift.

SelectNode.title: SelectNode
SelectNode.description: Join mutually exclusive record producers without guessing a winner.

self.title: Self
self.description: The text that backs the value.

SemanticAddress.title: SemanticAddress
SemanticAddress.description: Stable meaning identity, independent of source-line presentation.

ServerStopResult.title: ServerStopResult
ServerStopResult.description: Acknowledgement that this daemon will exit and release its state root.

field.title: Field
field.description: A field as orient names it, or its predicate.

role.title: Role
role.description: Only when the field permits more than one role.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: Default: the write's `because` as self evidence.

expect.title: Expect
expect.description: Compare-and-set: the value(s) you read, [] for none; else slot_changed.

SetChange.title: SetChange
SetChange.description: Replace a single-value field; contend=true contests it instead.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: Run every check up to the commit and write nothing.

accept.title: Accept
accept.description: if_allowed: accept in this call when policy lets you; never: only propose.

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate you read at (a git oid or a unique 12+ hex prefix). A set refuses if its slot changed since; default: the current head.

field.title: Field
field.description: A field as orient names it, or its predicate.

expect.title: Expect
expect.description: Compare-and-set: the value(s) you read, [] for none; else slot_changed.

observation.title: Observation
observation.description: Claim ID of the accepted observation that settles the prediction.

contract.description: Advanced: the exact contract reference; omit to resolve it from the route.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: Advanced: explicit observation or terminal evidence instead of observation.

SettleRequest.title: SettleRequest
SettleRequest.description:
Settle one prediction; usually just the observation's Claim ID.

The route names the prediction (its contract name or a bound window's
RSC-... id), so the daemon resolves the exact contract reference and, for a
bound window, its anchor event. ``contract``, ``trigger_event`` and
``evidence`` are the advanced forms: an exact reference, an explicit anchor,
or terminal evidence from a mandated settle run.

SettleScopeGap.title: SettleScopeGap
SettleScopeGap.description:
One reason a settle grant's scope left a change out, so the whole change proposed.

``basis`` is the changed value's evidence basis (``None`` when the change
carries none a grant can name).

ShapeField.title: ShapeField
ShapeField.description:
One shaped field: read ``from`` the current record (``$item.fields.<f>``,
``$item.key.<k>``), or a literal ``value``; ``as`` casts it explicitly.

ShapeFieldSpec.title: ShapeFieldSpec
ShapeFieldSpec.description:
One shaped field: read ``from`` the record (``$item.fields.<f>``/``$item.key.<k>``),
or a literal ``value``; ``as`` casts it explicitly.

ShownObject.title: ShownObject
ShownObject.description:
An object value, shown whole: ``object`` is the value itself, never cut.

The wrapper is what keeps an object value from reading as a marker: an
object Claim holding ``{"preview": "cover", "length": 600}`` is shown as
``{"object": {"preview": "cover", "length": 600}}`` and reads back as that
object. Nothing inside ``object`` is interpreted.

field.title: Field
field.description: A field as orient names it, or its predicate.

SlotRef.title: SlotRef
SlotRef.description: A Subject's field; value picks one of several live values.

relative_path.title: Relative Path
relative_path.description: The REAL on-disk component names the daemon read, kernel-confirmed.

requested_path.title: Requested Path
requested_path.description: The spelling the derived Source request asked for, when the daemon recorded one. Absent on receipts written before the real-name law; never a lookup key.

SourceReadReceipt.title: SourceReadReceipt
SourceReadReceipt.description: Daemon receipt independently attesting one bounded authorized file read.

StateCoordinate.title: StateCoordinate
StateCoordinate.description:
The operational state one change was evaluated against.

``subject`` names the records (``runtime_credential:<id>``,
``host_workspace:<instance>``, ...) and ``digest`` is the sha256 of their
canonical JSON. A commit carrying ``at`` recomputes it where it writes and
refuses ``cruxible.preview.state_moved`` when it differs.

StoppedAutomationV1.title: StoppedAutomationV1
StoppedAutomationV1.description:
Automation retired with a retired definition; live successors instead carry
Lines disabled and their Mandates propose-only.

SubjectAssignment.title: SubjectAssignment
SubjectAssignment.description:
The recorded inputs of a digest-named Subject's id (identity D1).

A ``minted`` Subject and a ``further_holder`` (a further holder of a ``hint``
kind's key) are named from the ``operation`` (the intent) and ``member`` (the
creation member) that create them; the boundary recomputes the id from what
is recorded here. A first holder of a key records nothing: its binding is its
key, and its id the key's rendering (suffixed by the key's digest when taken),
which the boundary recomputes from the key Claims and the parent.

SubjectAuthoringPayload.title: SubjectAuthoringPayload
SubjectAuthoringPayload.description:
A transition of an existing Subject (its successor, e.g. retiring it).

A new Subject is never authored this way: core names it, so it is created by
``SubjectCreationAuthoringPayload`` (its kind and key), and lowering refuses
a shell naming a Subject that does not exist (``subject_id_not_assigned``).

SubjectCreationAuthoringPayload.title: SubjectCreationAuthoringPayload
SubjectCreationAuthoringPayload.description:
Create one Subject by its kind and key; core assigns its id (identity D1).

``key`` holds the key parts of a keyed kind (each key ClaimType by predicate,
or by its last name under the kind) and is empty for a minted kind. Lowering
canonicalizes each value by its key ClaimType's form and looks the key up: no
live Subject holds it -- create; exactly one -- resolve to it, creating
nothing; several -- refuse (``key_ambiguous``). A creation writes the Subject
under the id core assigns (the readable rendering of the canonical key, or a
minted id) with one key Claim per part, citing ``source`` (the rationale as
the author's own words when absent). A cited existing section or file is a
working selection (``citation_role`` ``evidence``). ``located_at`` says
where own words (a ``SelfSourceBody``) stand, as a Claim's does: each key
Claim then cites one located own-words Capture. Omitted when unset.

key.title: Key
key.description: Key ClaimType (predicate or short name) -> value, or just the value when the kind has one key; omit for a minted kind. A pair's end is {"kind": "subject", "subject": ...}.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Why this Subject exists; the key Claims' self evidence.

create_new.title: Create New
create_new.description: Hint kinds only: create another Subject even though one holds this key (assert semantic.distinct_from between them); otherwise the key resolves to it.

SubjectInput.title: SubjectInput
SubjectInput.description:
Create one Subject: name its kind and its key; core assigns the id.

``key`` maps each key ClaimType of the kind's SubjectKind (by predicate, or by
its last name under the kind) to its value; omit it for a minted kind. A
pair kind's end (a Subject-valued key part) is a Subject object: an existing
Subject, or ``{subject_kind, key}`` naming one by key -- the live holder, or
the one a subject member of the same change set creates. The id is the
readable rendering of the canonical key (or a minted id), reported in the
result; the key parts become Claims citing ``rationale`` as your own words.

SubjectKeyPart.title: SubjectKeyPart
SubjectKeyPart.description:
One key part: the key ClaimType and its value.

A literal part's value is a string, an integer or a boolean. A
Subject-valued part (a pair kind's end) names the end as a Subject Claim
object, by one of the existing address forms: the Subject itself
(``artifact-v1``), the Subject a creation member of the same change lands on
(``subject-creation-v1``), or the Subject its kind's key names
(``subject-key-v1``). Lowering lands it on the end's path, which is the
part's canonical value.

SubjectKeyReference.title: SubjectKeyReference
SubjectKeyReference.description:
A Subject named by its kind's key: the one holding it, or the one a change creates.

A Procedure item names a Subject this way when the run has a key value but no
id: it resolves through the key index (and the aliases) to the existing
Subject, or to the Subject an item of the same terminal creates with that
key. ``key`` is the bare value for a one-key kind, or maps each key ClaimType
(by predicate, or by its last name under the kind) to its value. Both use
the key's canonical form and lower to the same governed mapping.

SubjectKindAuthoringPayload.title: SubjectKindAuthoringPayload
SubjectKindAuthoringPayload.description:
One SubjectKind decision: how core names Subjects of one kind.

Exactly one of ``keys`` (the key ClaimTypes by predicate, in key order, with
optional ``uniqueness``, default ``unique``) or ``minted``. ``normalizers``
names, per key part (by predicate or its last name under the kind), the
identity normalizer its value takes, pinned by version; a key part it does
not name takes ``none@1``, written out in the artifact. Lowering writes
``subject-kinds/<name>.json`` as the successor of the accepted one when there
is one; changing the keys, a normalizer or uniqueness is that governed
successor (a changed normalizer re-keys: the same change re-authors the key
values it moves), and no existing Subject's id moves.

name.title: Name
name.description: The Subject kind this declares, e.g. 'dev.decision'.

keys.title: Keys
keys.description: Key ClaimTypes by predicate, in key order; omit when minted.

normalizers.title: Normalizers
normalizers.description: Per key part (by predicate or last name), the identity normalizer its value takes, pinned by version: {normalizer: none|lowercase|pep503, version: 1}, or {normalizer: purl-type, version: 1, identity: package|package_variant}. A part not named takes none@1. Two raw values that normalize to one name one Subject.

uniqueness.title: Uniqueness
uniqueness.description: With keys: defaults to unique, which refuses a duplicate key; hint does not.

minted.title: Minted
minted.description: Core mints opaque ids; no keys.

predecessor_digest.title: Predecessor Digest
predecessor_digest.description: The digest of the accepted SubjectKind this succeeds, as you read it; the change refuses if the accepted one has moved since. Omit for a new kind.

SubjectKindInput.title: SubjectKindInput
SubjectKindInput.description:
How core names Subjects of one kind: by key ClaimTypes, or by minted ids.

Every new Subject is of a kind with an accepted SubjectKind. ``keys`` names
the key ClaimTypes (by predicate, in key order): each a ClaimType about
this kind only, literal and one-valued, accepted here or earlier; a Subject's
id is then the readable rendering of its canonical key. ``normalizers``
gives a key part an identity normalizer from the fixed core set. The default
``uniqueness: unique`` refuses a second live Subject with the same key; ``hint`` only
surfaces it in the duplicates audit. ``minted: true`` has core mint opaque
ids instead. Change it, or retire it, through a successor.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: kind/<id, alias or single key value>, or {subject_kind, key} naming the Subject by its kind's key (any number of key parts).

SubjectShell.title: SubjectShell
SubjectShell.description:
A stable referent with no mutable properties or free metadata.

``assignment`` is how core named a Subject created under a SubjectKind
(compiler revision 33); a Subject created before carries none.

SubjectSuccessionInput.title: SubjectSuccessionInput
SubjectSuccessionInput.description: A successor of an existing Subject's shell, e.g. retiring it (lifecycle retired).

SubjectType.title: SubjectType
SubjectType.description: A Subject of one of the explicitly named kinds, in canonical order.

claim.title: Claim
claim.description: A Claim ID (CLM-... or Claim:CLM-...); the daemon resolves its accepted version. An exact ClaimVersionReference object is accepted as the advanced form.

TransformAggregateSpec.title: TransformAggregateSpec
TransformAggregateSpec.description:
One value over the records: ``count``, ``any``/``all`` of ``where``, ``min``/``max`` of
``field``, or the ``first_by`` record ordered by ``field``.

TransformDeriveSpec.title: TransformDeriveSpec
TransformDeriveSpec.description:
``case [{when, value}] else value`` over named inputs (``$item.fields.<name>``).

The first case whose ``when`` is ``true`` decides; a ``when`` that is
``unknown`` before any case decides makes the derived value ``unknown``.
``else`` is required.

TransformFilterSpec.title: TransformFilterSpec
TransformFilterSpec.description: Keep the records whose closed predicate is ``true``; an ``unknown`` one taints the output.

TransformJoinSpec.title: TransformJoinSpec
TransformJoinSpec.description:
Records of ``left`` whose ``left_field`` equals a ``right`` record's ``right_field``.

``inner`` keeps each matched pair, adding ``right_fields`` (output name ->
right field); ``anti`` keeps the left records no right record matches.

TransformNode.title: TransformNode
TransformNode.description:
A closed, deterministic transform: records in, records (or one value) out.

Its records are typed as they flow (each field keeps its field result), its
predicates are three-valued, and its output carries completeness.

TransformRunSummary.title: TransformRunSummary
TransformRunSummary.description:
One closed transform: the records it read and the records it produced.

``rows_in`` sums every records input (a join's left and right, a union's
parts); ``rows_out`` is absent for a transform that produces one value
(``aggregate``, ``derive``), and ``rows_in`` for one that reads none.

TransformStep.title: TransformStep
TransformStep.description:
A closed transform (shape, filter, join, aggregate, dedupe, union, derive).

Its records are typed as they flow; it names no Contracts of its own.

anyOf.description: A registered internal action: floor.refresh, evidence.sweep, prediction.anchor_retry.

TriggerAuthoringPayload.title: TriggerAuthoringPayload
TriggerAuthoringPayload.description:
Decision-only Trigger input: a schedule and exactly one target.

``line_name`` names an accepted or same-set Line, which lowering refers to by
identity; ``action`` names an internal action instead.

line_name.title: Line Name
line_name.description: The Line this Trigger runs once that Line is enabled; omit when naming an action.

anyOf.description: A registered internal action: floor.refresh, evidence.sweep, prediction.anchor_retry.

action.title: Action
action.description: The internal action this Trigger fires; omit for a Line.

runbook_name.title: Runbook Name
runbook_name.description: The Runbook this Trigger runs (cadence, cron or generation_accepted); each Line step runs under that Line's own enablement.

TriggerInput.title: TriggerInput
TriggerInput.description:
One schedule aimed at an accepted or same-set Line, or a registered action.

Actions admit cadence, cron and generation_accepted. Every target's declared
input must be supplied by its schedule. Capture-based schedules name the
CaptureContract; prepare pins its digest. Exact event selectors are refused.
Retirement retains the predecessor's schedule and target without resolution.

TruncatedText.title: TruncatedText
TruncatedText.description:
A preview of a string value too long to show whole -- never the value itself.

``preview`` is the value's first ``GET_SUMMARY_TEXT_MAX_CHARS`` characters
and ``length`` its whole length. ``read_whole`` is the exact read of the
whole value when one Claim at one generation backs the preview (get cards,
history, query Claim cells and ``World.values``, a write's ``before``). A
plain query row cell has none: ask the query with ``claims=True`` and use
each Claim's preview; a write's ``after`` is the value the write sent.

VariantType.title: VariantType
VariantType.description: A tagged choice; each arm is one Contract version.

VerdictNotSupportedWarning.title: VerdictNotSupportedWarning
VerdictNotSupportedWarning.description:
The written Claim's verdict is not ``supported``; the write still lands.

For example ``uncovered``, because the ClaimType's evidence policy does not
admit the evidence given (R05). ``repair`` is the write again with admitted
evidence, and becomes the outcome's ``next``.

WholeValueRead.title: WholeValueRead
WholeValueRead.description:
The exact read that returns a preview's whole value.

``get(ref, detail="evidence", at=at)``: the Claim the preview came from, at
the accepted generation (``at``, its git oid) it was read at, so an older
revision or a value since replaced reads back as exactly what was previewed.
Its ``evidence.value`` is the whole value; the SDK's ``cx.read_whole(preview)``
makes this read.

WindowCloseAuthoringSchedule.title: WindowCloseAuthoringSchedule
WindowCloseAuthoringSchedule.description: Close a fixed window or resolve a named CaptureContract event anchor.

WorkingSourceObservation.title: WorkingSourceObservation
WorkingSourceObservation.description: One working source as a harness observed it, ready for the operation.

WorkspaceDetachResult.title: WorkspaceDetachResult
WorkspaceDetachResult.description:
One daemon host released from the Git worktree it was attached to.

The registry exclusivity is a UNIQUE index on (backend, workspace_root), so
a worktree can only ever be one host's. Moving one between hosts had no
verb: the refusal named "archive/rebuild that host", which is not a verb
either, and the rollback that does exactly this was reachable only from an
initialization failure.

WorkspaceFloorWriteResult.title: WorkspaceFloorWriteResult
WorkspaceFloorWriteResult.description: A verified floor export materialized by the workspace writer.

subjects_added.title: Subjects Added
subjects_added.description: The Subjects this write creates, by the id core assigned. A minted id (or a further hint holder's) is assigned when the write is submitted, so a dry run leaves it out.

coordinate.description: Accepted: the new generation. Otherwise the head this write was checked against; pass it back as `at` to pin a later write to it.

base.description: Accepted only: the head the write was checked against.

accepted_coordinate.description: The full accepted coordinate, when the request asked for it.

WriteOutcome.title: WriteOutcome
WriteOutcome.description: The answer to ``set``, ``retire`` and ``write``: an outcome, not a record.

change.title: Change
change.description: Index of the change in `changes` that refused.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: Run every check up to the commit and write nothing.

accept.title: Accept
accept.description: if_allowed: accept in this call when policy lets you; never: only propose.

at.title: At
at.description: The coordinate you read at (a git oid or a unique 12+ hex prefix). A set refuses if its slot changed since; default: the current head.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: The Subject every change that names none is about; a change's own subject overrides it.

doc_confirmations.title: Doc Confirmations
doc_confirmations.description: Writer-side acknowledgement of edits whose local file CAS succeeded.
